examples.en: I thought I wanted to become a person like that, too.

seeAlso: このような / そのような
こう / そう / ああ

pattern: それぞれ / それぞれのN
meaning: each; respectively; each one's own
formation: それぞれ + V / A (adverb)
それぞれ(の) + N
N + それぞれ
explanation: Shows that every member of a group is being considered individually, usually with the idea that each one is different. It can be used as an adverb or, with の, before a noun. Unlike みんな or 全部, which treat the group as one unit, それぞれ stresses the separate members. 一人一人 is similar but only for people; それぞれ works for people, places and things.

examples.ja: 学生たちはそれぞれ自分の意見を発表した。
examples.en: The students each presented their own opinion.

examples.ja: 国にはそれぞれの文化や習慣がある。
examples.en: Each country has its own culture and customs.

examples.ja: 三人はそれぞれ違う大学に入りました。
examples.en: The three of them each entered a different university.

meaning: it seems that ~; apparently ~; I hear that ~
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + らしい
Na / N + らしい (no だ)
Na / N + だった + らしい
N + らしい + N ('typical of N': 春らしい天気)
explanation: Reports a conjecture that rests on outside evidence: something you heard, read or observed. It sounds less personally committed than ようだ / みたいだ, which lean on your own direct impression, and less like a straight quotation than hearsay そうだ. Do not put だ before らしい in the present (学生らしい, not 学生だらしい). A separate use attaches to nouns to mean 'just what you expect of N', as in 子供らしい 'childlike'.

examples.ja: 田中さんは来月結婚するらしいです。
examples.en: Apparently Tanaka is getting married next month.

examples.ja: ニュースによると、昨日大阪で地震があったらしい。
examples.en: According to the news, it seems there was an earthquake in Osaka yesterday.

examples.ja: あの店のラーメンはとてもおいしいらしいよ。
examples.en: I hear the ramen at that shop is really good.

meaning: continue to ~; keep ~ing
formation: V(ます-stem) + 続ける
降り続く is the usual form for rain/snow (intransitive 続く)
explanation: Attaches to the verb stem to say that someone keeps an action going without stopping, usually by their own will or persistence. It conjugates like an ordinary る-verb (続けている, 続けた, 続けたい). 〜ている alone only says an action is in progress; 〜続ける adds the idea of duration and persistence. It is not used with momentary verbs such as 死ぬ or 着く for a single event.

examples.ja: 彼女は十年間、同じ会社で働き続けている。
examples.en: She has kept working at the same company for ten years.

examples.ja: 雨の中を二時間も歩き続けた。
examples.en: I kept walking in the rain for a whole two hours.

examples.ja: 夢があるなら、あきらめないで努力し続けてください。
examples.en: If you have a dream, please keep making an effort without giving up.

match: [いきしちにひみりぎじびえけせてねべめれげ](続|つづ)け

pattern: Nばかり / Vてばかりいる
meaning: only; nothing but ~; always doing ~
formation: N + ばかり (+ V) (replaces が/を; follows other particles: 〜にばかり)
V(て-form) + ばかりいる
N + ばかりだ
explanation: Says that there is so much of one thing, or one action is repeated so often, that it feels like nothing else exists. It is usually a complaint or criticism. だけ states a neutral limit ('only this, no more'), while ばかり gives the impression of 'too much of the same'. Do not mix it up with V(た)ばかり, which means 'just did'. ばっかり is the casual spoken form.

examples.ja: 弟は毎日ゲームをしてばかりいる。
examples.en: My younger brother does nothing but play games every day.

examples.ja: この店の客は若い女性ばかりだ。
examples.en: The customers at this shop are all young women.

examples.ja: 肉ばかり食べないで、野菜も食べなさい。
examples.en: Don't eat only meat; eat your vegetables too.

meaning: pure ~; completely ~; right in the middle of ~ (intensifying prefix)
formation: 真っ + colour / A stem: 真っ白, 真っ黒, 真っ暗, 真っ赤 (まっか), 真っ青 (まっさお)
真 + N: 真夜中, 真冬, 真夏, 真上, 真下
真ん + N: 真ん中, 真ん前
explanation: A prefix that pushes the meaning of a word to its extreme: 'pure white', 'pitch dark', 'the very middle'. The sound changes depending on the word (ま, まっ, まん), and a few forms are irregular (真っ赤 is まっか, 真っ青 is まっさお), so each word has to be learned as vocabulary. The results behave as な-adjectives or nouns: 真っ白な雪, 真っ暗になる. It cannot be attached freely to any adjective.

examples.ja: 朝起きたら、外は雪で真っ白だった。
examples.en: When I woke up in the morning, it was pure white outside with snow.

examples.ja: 真夜中に電話が鳴って、びっくりした。
examples.en: The phone rang in the middle of the night and startled me.

examples.ja: 彼は恥ずかしくて顔が真っ赤になった。
examples.en: He was so embarrassed that his face turned bright red.

match: 真(夜中|冬|夏|上|下|横|正面|新し)
まっ(しろ|くろ|さお|くら|すぐ)

meaning: that's why ~; no wonder ~; so it means that ~
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + わけだ
Na + な + わけだ
N + という / である + わけだ
explanation: Presents something as the natural, logical result of what has just been said or learned. It is used when you finally understand the reason for a situation ('no wonder'), when you draw a conclusion from facts ('so that means'), or when you restate things in other words. はずだ is a prediction about something not yet confirmed, whereas わけだ explains or accepts something already known to be true. Related forms have their own meanings: わけではない (not necessarily), わけがない (impossible), わけにはいかない (cannot very well do).

examples.ja: 彼は十年も日本に住んでいたのか。日本語が上手なわけだ。
examples.en: So he lived in Japan for ten years. No wonder his Japanese is good.

examples.ja: 窓が開いている。寒いわけだ。
examples.en: The window is open. That's why it's cold.

examples.ja: 今日は祝日だから、銀行が閉まっているわけです。
examples.en: Today is a national holiday, so that's why the banks are closed.

match: (わけ|訳)(だ|です|である|な(ん|の)(だ|です))

pattern: Nでよければ / Nでよかったら
meaning: if ~ is all right with you; if ~ will do
formation: N + で(も) + よければ / よかったら
N + で + よろしければ (more polite)
explanation: A modest way to make an offer or accept a request: you present something that may not be ideal and say 'if this is good enough'. で marks the thing as a sufficient condition, as in これでいい 'this will do'. It is typical when offering your own help, time or belongings (私でよければ). Using が instead (私がよければ) would mean 'if I am the best choice' and loses the humble tone.

examples.ja: 私でよければ、いつでも相談に乗りますよ。
examples.en: If I will do, I'm happy to give you advice any time.

examples.ja: 古い自転車でよければ、あげましょうか。
examples.en: If an old bicycle is all right, shall I give you one?

examples.ja: 明日でよろしければ、お手伝いできます。
examples.en: If tomorrow is all right with you, I can help.

match: で(も)?(よ|良)(ければ|かったら)

meaning: quite; fairly; rather (more than expected)
formation: 結構 + A / Na / adverb / V
結構な + N ('fine, splendid')
結構です ('that's fine' / 'no, thank you')
explanation: As an adverb, 結構 says that the degree is higher than you had assumed, though not extreme: 'more ~ than I thought'. It is conversational, usually written in kana in casual text, and used with both positive and negative qualities (結構高い). Because it implies you had low expectations, avoid using it to praise a superior's work directly. Keep it apart from the set phrase 結構です, which either accepts or politely refuses depending on context.

examples.ja: この映画、あまり期待していなかったけど、結構面白かった。
examples.en: I wasn't expecting much from this movie, but it was quite interesting.

examples.ja: 駅からここまで歩くと結構時間がかかりますよ。
examples.en: It takes a fair amount of time to walk here from the station.

examples.ja: 日本に来て、もう結構長くなりました。
examples.en: It has already been quite a while since I came to Japan.

meaning: quite; pretty; considerably (better than expected)
formation: なかなか + A / Na / adverb (affirmative)
なかなかの + N
explanation: In an affirmative sentence, なかなか is a positive evaluation: the quality is well above average or better than you expected. It is mostly used with favourable words (なかなかいい, なかなか上手だ) and sounds like an assessment from above, so do not use it about your teacher's or boss's ability. With a negative predicate the meaning changes completely to 'not easily' (なかなか来ない). 結構 is close but can also be used with unfavourable qualities.

examples.ja: この店のケーキはなかなかおいしいですね。
examples.en: The cake at this shop is pretty good, isn't it?

examples.ja: 彼の日本語はなかなか上手だ。
examples.en: His Japanese is quite good.

examples.ja: 初めてにしては、なかなかいい発表だった。
examples.en: For a first time, it was quite a good presentation.

meaning: speaking of which; come to think of it; that reminds me
formation: そう言えば、S
そういえば、S (kana spelling is very common)
explanation: Placed at the start of a sentence when something in the conversation, or a sudden thought, reminds you of a related matter. It lets you bring up a new topic smoothly without seeming abrupt. ところで changes to an unrelated topic on purpose, while そう言えば signals that the new topic was triggered by what was just said. It is conversational and not used in formal writing.

examples.ja: そう言えば、山田さんは最近どうしていますか。
examples.en: Speaking of which, how has Yamada been doing lately?

examples.ja: 「来週は連休だね。」「そう言えば、旅行の予約はもうした？」
examples.en: "Next week is a long weekend." "That reminds me, have you booked the trip yet?"

examples.ja: そういえば、今日は母の誕生日だった。
examples.en: Come to think of it, today is my mother's birthday.

pattern: 〜ということが分かる / 〜ということが考えられる
romaji: to iu koto ga wakaru / to iu koto ga kangaerareru
meaning: (find / think / hear) that ~; the fact that ~
formation: S(plain) + ということ + が / を / は / に + V
S + ということが分かる ('it turns out that')
S + ということが考えられる ('it can be thought that')
explanation: ということ wraps a whole statement into a noun so it can become the subject or object of verbs of knowing, thinking, hearing and reporting. Compared with plain こと, the という makes it clear that the content is a complete proposition, and it is required after だ (病気だということ). This pattern is a staple of reports and essays for stating findings and inferences. Do not confuse it with sentence-final 〜ということだ, which is hearsay or a restatement.

examples.ja: 調べてみて、この町には古いお寺が多いということが分かった。
examples.en: After looking into it, I found that this town has many old temples.

examples.ja: これらの結果から、若者の考え方が変わってきたということが考えられる。
examples.en: From these results, it can be thought that young people's way of thinking has been changing.

examples.ja: 彼が来月帰国するということを聞いて、驚いた。
examples.en: I was surprised to hear that he is going back to his country next month.

match: (という|っていう|と言う)(こと|事)(が|を|は|に|も)

pattern: では / それでは / じゃ(あ)
meaning: well then; in that case; so
formation: S1。では / それでは / じゃ(あ)、S2。
explanation: Sentence-initial connectors that take what has just been said or the present situation as a starting point and move on: to a conclusion, a suggestion, the next activity, or a goodbye. それでは and では are polite or formal (meetings, classes, announcements); じゃ and じゃあ are their everyday spoken forms. They differ from それから ('and then', simple sequence) because they mean 'given that, ...'. Do not mix them up with the particle combination では in 日本では.

examples.ja: みなさん、準備はいいですか。では、始めましょう。
examples.en: Is everyone ready? Well then, let's begin.

examples.ja: 「今日は都合が悪いんです。」「それでは、明日はどうですか。」
examples.en: "Today is not convenient for me." "In that case, how about tomorrow?"

examples.ja: じゃ、また来週。
examples.en: Well then, see you next week.

meaning: on top of that; moreover; what's more
formation: S1。その上、S2。
〜て、その上〜
explanation: Adds a further point that pushes in the same direction as what came before, either good on good or bad on bad. It is a little stronger and more formal than それに and suggests that the extra item goes beyond what would already have been enough. The two statements must share the same evaluation, so it cannot join a merit and a demerit. Clause-final 〜上(に) has the same meaning inside one sentence.

examples.ja: このアパートは駅から近い。その上、家賃も安い。
examples.en: This apartment is close to the station. On top of that, the rent is cheap.

examples.ja: 彼は頭がよくて、その上スポーツも得意だ。
examples.en: He is smart and, what's more, good at sports.

examples.ja: 道に迷って、その上雨まで降ってきた。
examples.en: I got lost, and on top of that it even started to rain.

meaning: even ~
formation: N + さえ (replaces が / を / は)
N + に / と / から / で + さえ
N + でさえ (often for a subject: 'even N')
explanation: Picks an extreme or least likely example to imply that everything else is naturally included: if even this is the case, the rest goes without saying. It is somewhat more written and emphatic than も used in the same way. Most sentences with さえ are negative or describe something surprising. Do not confuse it with the conditional 〜さえ〜ば ('if only ~, that is enough').

examples.ja: 忙しくて、昼ご飯を食べる時間さえない。
examples.en: I'm so busy that I don't even have time to eat lunch.

examples.ja: この漢字は日本人でさえ読めないことがある。
examples.en: Even Japanese people sometimes can't read this kanji.

examples.ja: 彼は親にさえ本当のことを話さなかった。
examples.en: He didn't tell the truth even to his parents.

meaning: intended for ~; aimed at ~; made for ~
formation: N + 向けだ
N + 向けの + N
N + 向けに + V
explanation: Says that a product, service or piece of content was deliberately designed with a certain group or destination as its target. N is the intended user or market: 子供向け, 女性向け, 海外向け. Compare N向き, which only says something happens to suit N whether or not it was planned that way (初心者向きの山 'a mountain suitable for beginners'). Also distinguish it from 〜に向けて, 'toward (a goal or direction)'.

examples.ja: これは子供向けの番組ですが、大人が見ても面白い。
examples.en: This is a program made for children, but it's interesting for adults too.

examples.ja: この会社は海外向けに日本のお菓子を売っている。
examples.en: This company sells Japanese sweets for the overseas market.

examples.ja: この教科書は初心者向けだ。
examples.en: This textbook is intended for beginners.

meaning: is; am; are (formal written copula, = だ)
formation: N / Na + である
N / Na + であった / ではない / であろう / であり、
N1 + である + N2 (modifying: 'N2, which is N1')
S(plain) + の + である (= のだ)
explanation: The written-style equivalent of だ, used in essays, academic papers, newspaper editorials and formal explanations. A text written in である style keeps plain forms throughout and does not mix in です/ます. である can do one thing だ cannot: stand directly before a noun (学生である田中さん) or before こと and の. It is not used in ordinary conversation, where it would sound stiff or pompous.

examples.ja: 日本は島国である。
examples.en: Japan is an island nation.

examples.ja: 漫画は今や日本を代表する文化の一つである。
examples.en: Manga is now one of the cultural forms that represent Japan.

examples.ja: これが事実であるかどうかは、まだ分からない。
examples.en: Whether or not this is a fact is not yet known.

meaning: suddenly start to ~; burst out ~ing; ~ out
formation: V(ます-stem) + 出す
explanation: With verbs of sound, emotion, movement and weather, 〜出す describes an action that begins abruptly or unexpectedly: 泣き出す, 笑い出す, 降り出す, 走り出す. V始める is a neutral 'begin' and can be used for planned actions, but 〜出す is not natural for your own deliberate plans or in requests (勉強し出してください is odd). With other verbs it keeps the literal sense of bringing something out or into existence, as in 取り出す, 思い出す, 作り出す.

examples.ja: 赤ちゃんが急に泣き出した。
examples.en: The baby suddenly burst out crying.

examples.ja: 空が暗くなって、雨が降り出した。
examples.en: The sky got dark and it started to rain.

examples.ja: その話を聞いて、みんな笑い出してしまった。
examples.en: Hearing that story, everyone burst out laughing.

match: [いきしちにひみりぎじびえけせてねべめれげ]出(す|し|さ|せ|そ)

romaji: nai wa nai / nai wa inai
meaning: there is no ~ that doesn't ~; every ~ does
formation: V(ない-form) + N + は + ない / いない
A(く)ない + N + はない
V(potential ない-form) + こと + はない
explanation: A double negative used to make a strong positive statement: 'there is nobody who doesn't know' means 'absolutely everyone knows'. Use いない when the noun is a person or animal and ない for things. It is more emphatic and rhetorical than simply saying みんな〜 or 何でも〜. Be careful not to read it as a negative sentence; the two negatives cancel out.

examples.ja: 日本でこのアニメを知らない人はいない。
examples.en: There is no one in Japan who doesn't know this anime.

examples.ja: 失敗しない人間はいないのだから、心配しなくてもいい。
examples.en: There is no human who never fails, so you don't need to worry.

examples.ja: 練習すれば、できないことはないと思う。
examples.en: If you practice, I think there is nothing you can't do.

keywords: there is no one who doesn't
match: ない[^、。はが]{1,6}は(い)?(ない|ません)

meaning: X corresponds to Y; X is equivalent to Y
formation: X + は + Y + に当たる
Y + に当たる + X
explanation: Used to say that something corresponds to something else in a different system: a word in another language, a rank, a unit, a date, or a family relationship. It does not claim the two are identical, only that one fills the same slot as the other. Note that 当たる has many other meanings (to hit, to win a prize, to be exposed to), so the context of comparison is what signals this use.

examples.ja: 日本の「部長」は英語の何に当たりますか。
examples.en: What does the Japanese word 'buchou' correspond to in English?

examples.ja: 一ドルは今、だいたい百五十円に当たる。
examples.en: One dollar is currently equivalent to roughly 150 yen.

examples.ja: 英語の「すみません」に当たる言葉を教えてください。
examples.en: Please tell me the English word that corresponds to 'sumimasen'.

meaning: it means that ~; it follows that ~; end up ~
formation: S(plain) + (という)ことになる
Na / N + (だ)ということになる
explanation: Draws a logical consequence: if the facts are as stated, then the situation amounts to this. It is common after conditions and calculations (〜ば、〜ことになる). This is different from the 'it has been decided that' use of 〜ことになった, which reports an arrangement made by others, although both share the idea of an outcome not chosen by the speaker. Adding という makes the reasoning sound more explicit.

examples.ja: 一日に二時間勉強すれば、一年で七百時間以上勉強したことになる。
examples.en: If you study two hours a day, it means you will have studied over 700 hours in a year.

examples.ja: 彼が来ないなら、私が一人で発表するということになる。
examples.en: If he doesn't come, it means I will end up presenting alone.

examples.ja: 全員が賛成したので、計画は決まったということになります。
examples.en: Since everyone agreed, it follows that the plan has been settled.

match: (という|っていう)(こと|事)にな(る|り|っ|ら)
[るいただ](こと|事)にな(る|り|っ|ら)

pattern: 〜(という)傾向がある / 〜傾向が見られる
romaji: (to iu) keikou ga aru / keikou ga mirareru
meaning: there is a tendency to ~; tend to ~
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + (という)傾向がある / 見られる
Na + な + 傾向がある
N + の + 傾向がある
explanation: An objective, report-like way to describe a general trend in a group, society or data. 傾向が見られる ('a tendency can be observed') is even more detached and is typical of surveys and academic writing. For everyday talk about individual habits, 〜がちだ or 〜やすい are more natural. The statement admits exceptions, so it is a good way to avoid over-generalizing.

examples.ja: 最近の若者はあまり新聞を読まない傾向がある。
examples.en: Young people these days tend not to read newspapers much.

examples.ja: 都会では一人で暮らす人が増えるという傾向が見られる。
examples.en: In cities, a tendency for the number of people living alone to increase can be seen.

examples.ja: 日本人ははっきり「いいえ」と言わない傾向があると言われている。
examples.en: It is said that Japanese people tend not to say 'no' clearly.

meaning: if we suppose that ~; supposing ~; if it were the case that ~
formation: (もし) + V / A(い) (plain) + としたら / とすれば / とすると
(もし) + Na / N + だ + としたら
explanation: Sets up an assumption, often an unreal or unverified one, and asks or states what would follow. It is more explicitly hypothetical than plain たら: the speaker is saying 'let us assume this is true'. Typical uses are imaginary questions (if you could be reborn...) and reasoning from an uncertain premise (if what he says is true...). もし is optional and simply announces the hypothesis early.

examples.ja: もし生まれ変われるとしたら、何になりたいですか。
examples.en: If you could be reborn, what would you want to be?

examples.ja: 一億円もらったとしたら、まず家を買うだろう。
examples.en: Supposing I received a hundred million yen, I would probably buy a house first.

examples.ja: 彼の話が本当だとしたら、大変なことになる。
examples.en: If what he says is true, it will be a serious matter.

pattern: Nが〜する (音がする / 頭がガンガンする)
meaning: feel ~ / there is a (sound, smell, taste, sensation)
formation: N(body part) + が + sound-symbolic word + する: 頭がガンガンする, 胸がドキドキする
N(音 / 声 / におい / 味 / 感じ) + が + する
explanation: する here is not 'to do' but 'to be perceived'. With a sound-symbolic word it describes a physical or emotional sensation in a part of the body (pounding head, racing heart, queasy stomach). With nouns of perception it reports that a sound, smell, taste or feeling is present. The perceived thing or body part is marked with が, never を. Choosing the right sound word is a matter of vocabulary: ガンガン for a throbbing head, ドキドキ for a beating heart, ムカムカ for nausea.

examples.ja: 風邪をひいて、頭がガンガンする。
examples.en: I caught a cold and my head is pounding.

examples.ja: 発表の前は、いつも胸がドキドキします。
examples.en: Before a presentation, my heart always pounds.

examples.ja: 台所からカレーのいいにおいがする。
examples.en: There is a nice smell of curry coming from the kitchen.

match: が(がんがん|ずきずき|どきどき|わくわく|むかむか|ふらふら|いらいら|くらくら)(する|し)
(音|におい|匂い|臭い|味|香り|声|感じ)が(する|し(ます|た|て|ない))

meaning: even though ~; and yet ~ (with blame or contempt)
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + くせに
Na + な + くせに
N + の + くせに
explanation: A strongly emotional 'although': the speaker criticizes or looks down on someone whose behaviour does not fit their situation, ability or position. Both clauses must have the same subject, and that subject is normally another person, not yourself. のに expresses surprise or disappointment and can be used for any contradiction; くせに adds accusation and is used in casual speech, complaints and teasing. It is rude if said to a superior.

examples.ja: 彼は何も知らないくせに、何でも知っているような顔をする。
examples.en: Even though he knows nothing, he acts as if he knows everything.

examples.ja: お金がないくせに、高い物ばかり買う。
examples.en: He has no money, and yet he buys nothing but expensive things.

examples.ja: 子供のくせに、大人みたいなことを言うね。
examples.en: You're just a kid, and yet you talk like an adult.

meaning: spoken contraction of 〜てしまう / 〜でしまう
formation: V(て-form): 〜てしまう → 〜ちゃう (食べてしまう → 食べちゃう)
V(で): 〜でしまう → 〜じゃう (読んでしまう → 読んじゃう)
past: 〜ちゃった / 〜じゃった; polite: 〜ちゃいます
explanation: In casual speech てしまう shrinks to ちゃう and でしまう to じゃう, keeping both meanings: doing something completely, and doing something unintentionally or regrettably. The result conjugates as a normal う-verb (ちゃった, ちゃって, ちゃわない). It is used among friends and family, in manga and in songs, but not in writing or formal situations. Do not confuse it with 〜ちゃ, the contraction of 〜ては as in 行っちゃだめ.

examples.ja: ごめん、君のケーキ、食べちゃった。
examples.en: Sorry, I went and ate your cake.

examples.ja: 早くしないと、電車が行っちゃうよ。
examples.en: If you don't hurry, the train will leave.

examples.ja: 面白くて、一晩で全部読んじゃった。
examples.en: It was so interesting that I read the whole thing in one night.

meaning: spoken contraction of 〜なければ(ならない) / 〜なくては(いけない): have to
formation: V(ない-form): 〜なければ → 〜なきゃ (+ ならない / いけない, often omitted)
V(ない-form): 〜なくては → 〜なくちゃ (+ いけない, often omitted)
〜ては → 〜ちゃ, 〜では → 〜じゃ: 行ってはだめ → 行っちゃだめ
explanation: Everyday spoken forms of 'must'. なければ becomes なきゃ and なくては becomes なくちゃ, and the final ならない or いけない is frequently dropped, so a sentence can simply end in なきゃ. They are often used when reminding yourself of something you need to do. The same sound change turns ては into ちゃ and では into じゃ in prohibitions. Keep the full forms for writing and polite speech.

examples.ja: もう十時だ。そろそろ帰らなきゃ。
examples.en: It's already ten. I have to head home soon.

examples.ja: 明日は試験だから、今晩勉強しなくちゃいけない。
examples.en: I have an exam tomorrow, so I have to study tonight.

examples.ja: 薬を飲むのを忘れないようにしなきゃ。
examples.en: I've got to make sure I don't forget to take my medicine.

match: なきゃ|なくちゃ|なくっちゃ

meaning: spoken contractions of 〜ている and 〜ておく
formation: 〜ている → 〜てる / 〜でいる → 〜でる (見ている → 見てる, 読んでいた → 読んでた)
〜ておく → 〜とく / 〜でおく → 〜どく (買っておく → 買っとく, 読んでおく → 読んどく)
〜という → 〜って; 〜のだ → 〜んだ
explanation: Spoken Japanese drops or merges vowels in very frequent auxiliaries. The い of ている disappears (してる, 知ってます), and ておく fuses into とく, which then conjugates normally (しといた, しといて). These forms are standard in relaxed conversation, even in です/ます speech for てる, but they are avoided in formal writing. Learners often miss them when listening, so it helps to recognise that 入れといた is 入れておいた.

examples.ja: 今、何してるの？
examples.en: What are you doing right now?

examples.ja: ビール、冷蔵庫に入れといたよ。
examples.en: I put the beer in the fridge for later.

examples.ja: あの人、知ってる？田中さんって言うんだ。
examples.en: Do you know that person? His name is Tanaka.

match: (って|んで|いて|いで|きて|ねて|みて)(る|た|ます(?!ます)|ない)(の|よ|ね|な|か|？|。|ん|けど|から|し|っけ|人|時|こと|$)
[^決たうとそ]して(る|た|ます(?!ます)|ない)(の|よ|ね|な|か|？|。|ん|けど|から|し|っけ|人|時|こと|$)
[えけせてねべめれげっんしい](と|ど)い(た|て)

pattern: 〜(という)わけではない / 〜わけじゃない
romaji: (to iu) wake dewa nai / wake ja nai
meaning: it's not that ~; it doesn't mean that ~; not necessarily ~
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + (という)わけではない
Na + な / だという + わけではない
N + という + わけではない
explanation: Denies a conclusion that the listener might naturally draw from the situation or from what was just said. It is a partial or soft denial: 'I don't mean X exactly'. It often appears with 全部, みんな, いつも or 必ずしも to say 'not all / not always', and is typically followed by が or けど and a clarification. A flat 〜ない simply negates the fact, while わけではない negates the inference. Do not confuse it with わけがない ('there is no way that').

examples.ja: 日本人がみんな寿司が好きだというわけではない。
examples.en: It's not the case that all Japanese people like sushi.

examples.ja: 嫌いなわけじゃないけど、あまり食べません。
examples.en: It's not that I dislike it, but I don't eat it much.

examples.ja: 高ければいいというわけではありません。
examples.en: It doesn't mean that something is good just because it is expensive.

match: (わけ|訳)(では|じゃ|でも)(ない|ありません|なく|なかっ)

meaning: while ~ (before the state changes); before ~
formation: V(dictionary / ている / ない-form) + うちに
A(い) + うちに
Na + な + うちに
N + の + うちに
explanation: Marks a period that will come to an end and says something should be done, or something happens, before it does. With a state (若い, 熱い, 学生の) it carries urgency: do it now, because later will be too late. With ない it means 'before X happens' (忘れないうちに). With ている it can also describe a change that occurs unnoticed during an activity (話しているうちに). 間に just marks a time span, without the sense of a closing window.

examples.ja: 熱いうちに食べてください。
examples.en: Please eat it while it's hot.

examples.ja: 日本にいるうちに、富士山に登ってみたい。
examples.en: While I'm in Japan, I'd like to try climbing Mt. Fuji.

examples.ja: 暗くならないうちに帰りましょう。
examples.en: Let's go home before it gets dark.

pattern: XはYと関係がある / XとYに(は)関係がある
romaji: to kankei ga aru / ni kankei ga aru
meaning: X is related to Y; X has something to do with Y
formation: X + は + Y + と / に + 関係がある / ない
X + と + Y + (の間)に(は) + 関係がある
Y + と関係がある / 関係のある + N
explanation: States that a connection of some kind exists between two things, without saying exactly what kind; modifiers such as 深い, 強い or 密接な can be added before 関係. The negative 関係がない is the standard way to say 'has nothing to do with' or 'is none of my business' (私には関係がない). Before a noun, が may change to の (関係のある人). For 'regardless of', use the separate pattern 〜に関係なく.

examples.ja: 歌舞伎は江戸時代の町人文化と深い関係がある。
examples.en: Kabuki is deeply related to the townspeople's culture of the Edo period.

examples.ja: この事件は私には関係がありません。
examples.en: This incident has nothing to do with me.

examples.ja: 食べ物と健康には強い関係があると言われている。
examples.en: It is said that there is a strong relationship between food and health.

match: 関係(が|の|は|も)(深い|強い)?(ある|あり|あっ|ない|なか|なく)

meaning: by (means of) ~; because of ~; by (agent of a passive)
formation: N + によって / により
V(dictionary) + こと + によって
N + による + N
explanation: A formal expression with three main jobs: showing the means or method by which a result is achieved, showing the cause of an event, and marking the doer in a passive sentence, especially for creating, building or discovering. To use a verb as the means, nominalize it with こと. In everyday speech で or から would do the first two jobs; によって belongs to written and explanatory style. A fourth meaning, 'depending on' (人によって違う), is the same form with a different function.

examples.ja: インターネットによって、世界中の情報が簡単に手に入るようになった。
examples.en: Through the internet, it has become easy to get information from all over the world.

examples.ja: 毎日声を出して読むことによって、発音がよくなる。
examples.en: By reading aloud every day, your pronunciation improves.

examples.ja: この寺は八世紀に有名な僧によって建てられた。
examples.en: This temple was built in the eighth century by a famous monk.

meaning: then; thereupon; if that is so, then ~
formation: S1。すると、S2。
explanation: A sentence-initial connector with two uses. In narration it introduces what happened or what was discovered right after the first action, usually something the subject did not control, so the second sentence cannot express the speaker's own intention. In conversation it draws an inference from what the other person said: 'so that means...'. そして simply adds the next event, while すると implies the second event was triggered by, or revealed through, the first.

examples.ja: ドアを開けた。すると、知らない男の人が立っていた。
examples.en: I opened the door. Then I found a man I didn't know standing there.

examples.ja: ボタンを押してみた。すると、急に音楽が流れ出した。
examples.en: I tried pressing the button. Thereupon, music suddenly started playing.

examples.ja: 「彼は昨日から熱があるそうです。」「すると、今日の会議には出られませんね。」
examples.en: "I hear he has had a fever since yesterday." "Then he won't be able to attend today's meeting, will he?"

meaning: as ~; just as ~; in the way that ~; according to ~
formation: V(dictionary / た-form) + 通り(に)
N + の + 通り(に)
N + 通り(に) (read どおり: 予定通り, 希望通り)
〜通りの + N / 〜通りだ
explanation: Says that something is done or turns out exactly the same as a model: instructions, a plan, an expectation, or what someone said or did. When attached directly to a noun without の, the reading changes to どおり. ように also means 'as' but allows loose resemblance; 通り insists on matching the original faithfully. Common set phrases include その通りです ('exactly right') and 思った通り ('just as I thought').

examples.ja: 先生が言った通りに書いてください。
examples.en: Please write it exactly as the teacher said.

examples.ja: 説明書の通りに作ったのに、うまく動かない。
examples.en: I built it according to the instructions, but it doesn't work well.

examples.ja: 試合は予想通り、日本チームが勝った。
examples.en: As expected, the Japanese team won the match.

match: (た|る|の)(通|とお)り(に|の|だ|です|、|で)
(?![大表裏])[一-龠](通|どお)り(に|の|だ|です|、)

meaning: the more ~, the more ~
formation: V(ば-form) + V(dictionary) + ほど
A(い→ければ) + A(い) + ほど
Na + なら(ば) + Na + な + ほど / Na + であればあるほど
N + であればあるほど
explanation: Expresses that as one thing increases in degree, another changes in proportion. The same word is said twice, first in the ば-form and then in the dictionary form before ほど. The first half can be dropped in casual use (勉強するほど分かる). For する-verbs, only する is repeated: 練習すればするほど. The second clause normally describes a change or a degree, not a one-time action.

examples.ja: 日本語は勉強すればするほど面白くなる。
examples.en: The more you study Japanese, the more interesting it gets.

examples.ja: 家賃は駅に近ければ近いほど高い。
examples.en: The closer to the station, the higher the rent.

examples.ja: 考えれば考えるほど分からなくなってきた。
examples.en: The more I think about it, the less I understand.

match: (.{1,3})(れば|えば|けば|せば|てば|ねば|べば|めば|げば|ければ|ならば|なら)\1.{0,3}ほど

meaning: well; now; so (moving to a new topic or action)
formation: さて、S。
explanation: Used at the very start of a sentence to signal a shift: to the main subject, to the next item, or to an action the speaker is about to begin. It is common in speeches, lectures, letters and news programmes, and also when talking to yourself before starting something. Unlike ところで, which opens an unrelated side topic, さて moves the talk forward along its planned course. It is never used in the middle of a clause.

examples.ja: さて、次の問題に進みましょう。
examples.en: Now, let's move on to the next question.

examples.ja: これで説明は終わりです。さて、何か質問はありますか。
examples.en: That is the end of the explanation. Now then, are there any questions?

examples.ja: さて、今晩は何を食べようか。
examples.en: Well now, what shall I eat tonight?

pattern: Nを中心に(する) / Nを中心とするN
romaji: wo chuushin ni (suru) / wo chuushin to suru
meaning: centering on ~; focusing on ~; mainly ~
formation: N + を中心に(して) + V
N + を中心とする / とした / にした + N
N + が中心だ
explanation: Names the thing, person or place that is the core of an activity, group or range, with other things arranged around it. It can be physical (a region centred on Tokyo), organizational (a team centred on the captain) or about emphasis (a class focusing on conversation). The に form modifies a verb, while とする / とした modifies a noun. It implies that N is the main part but not the only one.

examples.ja: この授業は会話を中心に進められます。
examples.en: This class is conducted with a focus on conversation.

examples.ja: 台風は九州を中心に大きな被害を出した。
examples.en: The typhoon caused great damage, mainly in Kyushu.

examples.ja: 東京を中心とした地域には、三千万人以上が住んでいる。
examples.en: More than thirty million people live in the region centred on Tokyo.

pattern: 逆に / 逆のN / 逆だ
romaji: gyaku ni / gyaku no / gyaku da
meaning: opposite; reverse; conversely; on the contrary
formation: 逆に + S / V
逆の + N
N + と(は)逆だ / 逆に
逆 + N (compound: 逆効果, 逆方向)
explanation: 逆 means the reverse in direction, order, position or expected result. As the adverb 逆に it introduces an outcome that is the opposite of what was intended or expected ('instead, it got worse'), or turns the viewpoint around. 反対 overlaps for directions and positions but also means 'opposition, objection', which 逆 does not. 逆に in casual speech is also used loosely like 'actually' or 'if anything'.

examples.ja: 薬を飲んだら、逆に気分が悪くなった。
examples.en: When I took the medicine, I felt worse instead.

examples.ja: 駅はそっちじゃないよ。逆の方向だ。
examples.en: The station isn't that way. It's the opposite direction.

examples.ja: 弟は私とは逆で、とても静かな性格だ。
examples.en: My younger brother is the opposite of me; he has a very quiet personality.

match: 逆(に|の|で|だ|です|方向|効果|さま)|ぎゃくに

meaning: should ~; ought to ~; be supposed to ~; I expect that ~
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + はずだ
Na + な + はずだ
N + の + はずだ
〜はずがない ('cannot possibly') / 〜はずだった ('was supposed to') / 〜はずなのに
explanation: Expresses the speaker's confident expectation based on reasons such as schedules, logic or memory: things ought to be so. It is not used for moral duty ('you should apologize' is べきだ or たほうがいい) and not for the speaker's own intentions. 〜はずなのに and 〜はずだった show that reality did not match the expectation. Compared with わけだ, which explains a known fact, はずだ predicts something not yet confirmed.

examples.ja: 荷物は昨日送ったから、今日着くはずです。
examples.en: I sent the package yesterday, so it should arrive today.

examples.ja: 彼は十年もアメリカに住んでいたから、英語が上手なはずだ。
examples.en: He lived in America for ten years, so his English ought to be good.

examples.ja: ここに置いたはずなのに、鍵が見つからない。
examples.en: I'm sure I put it here, but I can't find the key.

match: はず(だ|です|の|な|が|は|で|も)|筈

meaning: point; respect; aspect; in that ~
formation: S(plain) + (という)点 + で / が / は / に
Na + な + 点 / N + の + 点
この / その / どの + 点
explanation: 点 turns a description into 'the point that ~' so you can compare, praise or criticize one specific aspect of something. 〜という点で means 'in the respect that', and is the usual way to say in what way two things are alike or different. Use it for abstract aspects, not physical spots (those are 所). いい点 / 悪い点 are 'good points / bad points'.

examples.ja: この二つの言葉は、意味が似ているという点で間違えやすい。
examples.en: These two words are easy to confuse in that their meanings are similar.

examples.ja: 値段が安い点はいいが、質はあまりよくない。
examples.en: The point that it is cheap is good, but the quality isn't very good.

examples.ja: 落語は一人で演じるという点が、ほかの演劇と違う。
examples.en: Rakugo differs from other theatre in the respect that it is performed by one person.

meaning: more and more; increasingly; even more
formation: ますます + V (change) / A(く) + なる / Na + に + なる
ますます + A / adverb
explanation: An adverb showing that a degree which was already notable keeps rising. It is used with verbs of change (増える, 進む, 〜くなる) and with adjectives and adverbs. It leans slightly formal and is common in news and essays; in conversation もっと or どんどん may replace it, although どんどん stresses speed and momentum rather than degree. It is not used with one-time actions.

examples.ja: 十二月に入って、ますます寒くなってきた。
examples.en: Now that it's December, it has become colder and colder.

examples.ja: 練習を続けたら、テニスがますます面白くなった。
examples.en: As I kept practicing, tennis became even more fun.

examples.ja: 外国から来る観光客は、これからますます増えるだろう。
examples.en: The number of tourists from abroad will probably increase more and more from now on.

meaning: have a feeling that ~; it feels like ~; I sort of think ~
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + (ような)気がする
Na + な + (ような)気がする
N + の + ような気がする
〜気がしない ('don't feel that / can't imagine')
explanation: States a vague impression or intuition that the speaker cannot fully back up, softer than と思う. Adding ような makes it even less assertive. It is often used to give an opinion gently or to describe a hunch or a hazy memory. 〜気がしない says you cannot bring yourself to feel something is so. Do not confuse it with 気がつく (notice) or 気になる (be bothered by, be curious about).

examples.ja: あの人には前にどこかで会ったような気がする。
examples.en: I have a feeling I've met that person somewhere before.

examples.ja: 今日は何かいいことがありそうな気がします。
examples.en: I have a feeling something good is going to happen today.

examples.ja: この問題は、何度考えても分かる気がしない。
examples.en: No matter how many times I think about this problem, I don't feel I'll ever get it.

match: 気が(する|し(ます|た|て|ない|ません))

romaji: koto wa ga / koto wa keredo
meaning: it's true that ~, but ...; I did ~ all right, but ...
formation: V(plain) + ことは + same V + が / けれど
A(い) + ことは + same A + が / けれど
Na + な + ことは + Na + だ + が / けれど
explanation: Repeats the same verb or adjective on both sides of ことは to admit that something is technically true before adding a reservation. The message is in the second half: the result is limited, unsatisfactory or comes with a problem. The first word is usually non-past even for past events (行くことは行った is as common as 行ったことは行った). It is a polite way to give a lukewarm answer without flatly saying no.

examples.ja: 歌舞伎は見たことは見たが、意味はよく分からなかった。
examples.en: I did see kabuki, but I didn't really understand what it meant.

examples.ja: このかばんは高いことは高いけれど、とても丈夫だ。
examples.en: This bag is expensive, to be sure, but it is very sturdy.

examples.ja: 漢字は読めることは読めますが、書くのは苦手です。
examples.en: I can read kanji all right, but I'm bad at writing them.

meaning: thanks to ~; owing to ~ (good result)
formation: N + の + おかげで / おかげだ
V / A(い) (plain) + おかげで
Na + な + おかげで
おかげさまで (set phrase: 'thanks to you / fortunately')
explanation: Gives the cause of a favourable result and expresses gratitude toward it. The cause is usually a person's help or a fortunate circumstance. Its negative twin is せいで, which blames a cause for a bad result. おかげで can be used sarcastically for a bad outcome (君のおかげで遅刻した), but the default reading is positive. ために states a neutral cause with no feeling attached.

examples.ja: 先生のおかげで、大学に合格できました。
examples.en: Thanks to my teacher, I was able to get into university.

examples.ja: 友達が手伝ってくれたおかげで、仕事が早く終わった。
examples.en: Thanks to my friend helping me, the work was finished early.

examples.ja: 日本語が上手になったのは、ホストファミリーのおかげだ。
examples.en: It is thanks to my host family that my Japanese got better.

romaji: sei de / sei da / sei ka
meaning: because of ~; due to ~ (bad result, blame)
formation: N + の + せいで / せいだ
V / A(い) (plain) + せいで
Na + な + せいで
〜せいか ('perhaps because ~')
explanation: Points to the cause of an undesirable result and assigns blame to it. The cause can be a person, an event or a condition. 〜のせいにする means 'to put the blame on', and 〜せいか softens the claim to 'maybe it's because'. Use おかげで when the result is good. Because it is accusatory, saying あなたのせいで to someone directly is a strong statement.

examples.ja: 雨のせいで、試合が中止になった。
examples.en: Because of the rain, the game was cancelled.

examples.ja: 昨日遅くまで起きていたせいで、今日は眠くてしかたがない。
examples.en: Because I stayed up late yesterday, I'm unbearably sleepy today.

examples.ja: 失敗したのは君のせいじゃないよ。
examples.en: It's not your fault that it failed.

match: (の|た|い|る|な)せい(で|だ|か|に|じゃ|では|です|なの)

meaning: rapidly; steadily; one after another; without hesitation
formation: どんどん + V
explanation: An adverb for actions or changes that proceed quickly and with momentum, without pause. With verbs of change it means 'rapidly, more and more'; with volitional actions it means 'freely, without holding back', which is why it is often used to encourage (どんどん食べてください). だんだん describes slow, gradual change, and ますます focuses on increasing degree; どんどん is about pace and force. It modifies verbs, not adjectives directly.

examples.ja: この町の人口はどんどん減っている。
examples.en: The population of this town is decreasing rapidly.

examples.ja: 分からないことがあったら、どんどん質問してください。
examples.en: If there is anything you don't understand, please go ahead and ask as many questions as you like.

examples.ja: 子供はどんどん新しい言葉を覚えていく。
examples.en: Children pick up new words one after another.

meaning: every time ~; whenever ~
formation: V(dictionary) + たびに
N + の + たびに
explanation: Says that on each occasion one thing happens, the same other thing also happens. The verb before たびに is always in the dictionary form, even for past events. Compared with 〜と or 〜時はいつも, it emphasizes the repetition one occasion at a time and often carries feeling such as nostalgia or annoyance. It is not used for natural laws or constant, automatic results (春になるたびに花が咲く is odd; use と).

examples.ja: この歌を聞くたびに、高校時代を思い出す。
examples.en: Every time I hear this song, I remember my high school days.

examples.ja: 父は出張のたびに、お土産を買ってきてくれる。
examples.en: My father buys me a souvenir every time he goes on a business trip.

examples.ja: 彼女は会うたびにきれいになっている。
examples.en: She gets prettier every time I see her.

match: (る|う|く|ぐ|す|つ|ぬ|ぶ|む|の)(たび|度)(に|ごとに)

meaning: finally; at last; in the end
formation: とうとう + V(past / ている)
とうとう + V(ない-form past) ('never did, in the end')
explanation: Marks the final outcome of a long process or wait. The outcome may be good or bad, and may be something that never happened (とうとう来なかった). やっと is used only for a hoped-for result achieved after difficulty and carries relief, whereas とうとう simply notes that the end point has been reached, often with a sense of 'it has come to this'. ついに is a more formal synonym.

examples.ja: 三年かかって、とうとう論文を書き終えた。
examples.en: It took three years, but I finally finished writing my thesis.

examples.ja: 長い間使っていたパソコンが、とうとう壊れてしまった。
examples.en: The computer I had used for a long time has finally broken.

examples.ja: 一時間待ったが、彼はとうとう来なかった。
examples.en: I waited an hour, but in the end he never came.

meaning: whether or not ~; whether ~ or not
formation: V(て-form) + も + V(ない-form → なくて) + も
A(い→くて) + も + A(く)なくて + も
Na / N + でも + Na / N + じゃなくても / でなくても
explanation: Pairs the affirmative and negative ても-forms of the same word to say that the result is the same in either case. The main clause states what holds regardless. For ある the negative half is simply なくても (あってもなくても). It is a specific case of 〜ても〜ても ('whether X or Y'), and close in meaning to 〜かどうかに関係なく, which is more formal.

examples.ja: 雨が降っても降らなくても、明日は出かけます。
examples.en: Whether it rains or not, I'm going out tomorrow.

examples.ja: テストがあってもなくても、毎日勉強したほうがいい。
examples.en: Whether there is a test or not, you should study every day.

examples.ja: 値段が高くても高くなくても、必要な物は買うしかない。
examples.en: Whether the price is high or not, I have no choice but to buy what I need.

meaning: the former ~, the latter ~
formation: A と B。前者は〜、後者は〜。
前者 = the first of two things mentioned; 後者 = the second
explanation: A written-style device for referring back to two items just mentioned without repeating their names: 前者 is the first one and 後者 the second. It is found in essays, textbooks and reports that compare two things. They are used only when exactly two items have been introduced, and both do not have to appear; 後者 alone is fine. In conversation people would simply repeat the nouns or use こっち / そっち.

examples.ja: 日本には公立高校と私立高校がある。前者は授業料が安いが、後者は高い。
examples.en: Japan has public high schools and private high schools. The former have low tuition, while the latter are expensive.

examples.ja: ひらがなとカタカナのうち、前者は主に日本語の言葉に、後者は外来語に使われる。
examples.en: Of hiragana and katakana, the former is used mainly for Japanese words and the latter for loanwords.

meaning: N such as ~; N like ~
formation: N1 (や / 、/ とか) N2 + といった + N
N1 + といった + N
explanation: Gives representative examples and then names the category they belong to. It implies the list is not complete. The meaning is close to 〜などの and 〜のような, but といった sounds more written and is normal in explanations, articles and presentations. The noun after it must be a general term that covers the examples (countries, subjects, problems). Written in kana, it should not be confused with と言った 'said that'.

examples.ja: この大学には中国や韓国といったアジアの国からの留学生が多い。
examples.en: This university has many international students from Asian countries such as China and Korea.

examples.ja: 数学、物理といった科目が苦手です。
examples.en: I'm not good at subjects like math and physics.

examples.ja: すしや天ぷらといった日本料理は海外でも人気がある。
examples.en: Japanese dishes such as sushi and tempura are popular overseas too.

meaning: on the other hand; while ~; whereas
formation: S1。一方(で)、S2。
V / A(い) (plain) + 一方(で)、〜
Na + な / である + 一方(で)
N + である + 一方(で)
explanation: Sets two facts side by side: either contrasting situations in two different subjects, or two different sides of the same subject. It is neutral and objective, typical of reports and news. It can join clauses or start a new sentence. Do not confuse it with V(dictionary) + 一方だ, which means 'keeps on ~ing (in one direction)', as in 増える一方だ.

examples.ja: 日本では子供の数が減っている。一方、お年寄りの数は増え続けている。
examples.en: In Japan the number of children is decreasing. On the other hand, the number of elderly people keeps growing.

examples.ja: この仕事は給料が高い一方で、休みがほとんどない。
examples.en: This job pays well, while on the other hand there are almost no days off.

examples.ja: 都会は便利な一方、家賃が高い。
examples.en: Cities are convenient, but on the other hand rents are high.

meaning: or; or else; or perhaps
formation: N1、あるいは N2
S1 か、あるいは S2 か
S1。あるいは、S2 (かもしれない)。
explanation: A formal 'or' for presenting alternatives between nouns, clauses or sentences. It is used in writing, announcements and careful speech where conversation would use か, それとも or または. Unlike それとも, it is not limited to questions. It can also work as an adverb meaning 'possibly', usually with かもしれない. または is very close in meaning; あるいは sounds slightly more literary.

examples.ja: 電話、あるいはメールでご連絡ください。
examples.en: Please contact us by phone or by email.

examples.ja: 卒業後は日本で就職するか、あるいは国に帰るか、まだ決めていない。
examples.en: I haven't yet decided whether to get a job in Japan after graduating or to go back to my country.

examples.ja: 彼は来ないかもしれない。あるいは、もう来ているのかもしれない。
examples.en: He might not come. Or perhaps he is already here.

meaning: not easily ~; not readily ~; takes a long time to ~
formation: なかなか + V(ない-form)
なかなか + V(potential ない-form)
explanation: With a negative verb, なかなか says that something you expect or want to happen is slow in coming or hard to achieve, in spite of waiting or trying. It often goes with potential verbs (なかなか覚えられない) and with verbs of arrival and change (来ない, 治らない). This is the opposite flavour from affirmative なかなか ('quite good'). あまり〜ない is about low frequency or degree, whereas なかなか〜ない is about difficulty and delay.

examples.ja: バスがなかなか来ないので、タクシーで行くことにした。
examples.en: The bus just wouldn't come, so I decided to go by taxi.

examples.ja: 漢字がなかなか覚えられなくて困っています。
examples.en: I'm having trouble because I can't easily memorize kanji.

examples.ja: 夜、コーヒーを飲んだら、なかなか眠れなかった。
examples.en: I drank coffee at night and then couldn't get to sleep for a long time.

match: なかなか[^。、]{0,15}(ない|なく|なかっ|ません|ず)

meaning: in other words; that is to say; in short
formation: N1、つまり N2
S1。つまり、S2 (ということだ / わけだ)。
explanation: Introduces a restatement of what was just said in clearer or more concise terms, or states the conclusion that follows from it. The sentence it introduces often ends in ということだ or わけだ. It can also be used to press someone for the bottom line ('so what you mean is...'). 要するに summarizes a long explanation; すなわち is a more formal 'namely'. It is not used to add new information.

examples.ja: 彼は父の兄の息子、つまり私のいとこです。
examples.en: He is my father's older brother's son, in other words my cousin.

examples.ja: この学校は月曜日から土曜日まで授業がある。つまり、休みは日曜日だけだ。
examples.en: This school has classes from Monday to Saturday. That is to say, the only day off is Sunday.

examples.ja: 「今回は難しいですね。」「つまり、だめだということですか。」
examples.en: "It's difficult this time." "In other words, you mean it's a no?"

meaning: so; therefore; that's why (I decided to ~)
formation: S1 (situation / problem)。そこで、S2 (action taken in response)。
explanation: Connects a situation or problem to the deliberate step someone takes in response to it. The second sentence must be a volitional action, a decision, a request or a proposal, not a natural result or a feeling. それで can introduce any kind of consequence, and だから gives a reason for a judgment; そこで specifically means 'given that situation, here is what was done'. It is common in narratives and presentations.

examples.ja: 一人ではできそうになかった。そこで、友達に手伝ってもらうことにした。
examples.en: It didn't look like I could do it alone. So I decided to have a friend help me.

examples.ja: 最近、体の調子がよくない。そこで、毎朝走ることにした。
examples.en: I haven't been feeling well lately. So I decided to go running every morning.

examples.ja: 日本語の会話が上手にならない。そこで、先生に相談してみた。
examples.en: My spoken Japanese isn't improving. So I tried consulting my teacher.

meaning: other than ~; except ~; besides ~
formation: N + 以外 + の + N / に / は / で
V(plain) + 以外(に) + (〜ない)
N + 以外に(も) ('in addition to')
explanation: Sets one item aside and talks about everything else. With a negative predicate it means 'nothing but, no one except' (彼以外は知らない). With も or an affirmative predicate it can mean 'besides, in addition to' (日本語以外にも). After a verb, 〜以外にない / 〜以外に方法がない means there is no alternative. ほかに is a looser everyday synonym; 以外 is a little more formal and precise.

examples.ja: 日曜日以外は毎日アルバイトをしています。
examples.en: I work part-time every day except Sunday.

examples.ja: この部屋には関係者以外入ることができません。
examples.en: No one other than authorized people can enter this room.

examples.ja: 自分でやる以外に方法がない。
examples.en: There is no way other than doing it myself.

meaning: never ~; by no means ~; definitely not ~
formation: 決して + V(ない-form)
決して + A(く)ない
決して + Na / N + ではない
explanation: An adverb that always pairs with a negative and makes the denial strong and absolute. It is used for firm resolutions (決して忘れない), prohibitions and emphatic corrections of a possible misunderstanding (決して安くはない). It is somewhat formal; in conversation 絶対に〜ない is more common. It does not express low frequency by itself, so for 'I have never done' use 一度も〜たことがない.

examples.ja: あの日のことは決して忘れません。
examples.en: I will never forget that day.

examples.ja: 彼は決して悪い人ではない。
examples.en: He is by no means a bad person.

examples.ja: この試験は決して簡単ではなかった。
examples.en: This exam was definitely not easy.

meaning: for the reason that ~; on the grounds that ~
formation: S(plain) + という理由で
N (+ だ) + という理由で
〜という理由から / 〜という理由により (more formal)
explanation: Spells out the reason, often the officially stated or claimed one, behind a decision or action. Because it quotes the reason with という, it can keep some distance: the speaker reports the grounds given without necessarily agreeing. It is common in news and formal explanations, especially for refusals, dismissals and cancellations. Plain から / ので simply give the speaker's own reason.

examples.ja: 彼は体の調子が悪いという理由で、会社を辞めた。
examples.en: He quit the company for the reason that he was in poor health.

examples.ja: 高すぎるという理由で、その計画は中止になった。
examples.en: The plan was cancelled on the grounds that it was too expensive.

examples.ja: 子供だという理由で、意見を聞いてもらえなかった。
examples.en: My opinion wasn't listened to for the reason that I was a child.

match: (という|との|っていう)理由(で|から|により)

meaning: plural marker for people and demonstratives
formation: pronoun + ら: 彼ら, 彼女ら, 僕ら, 俺ら, 私ら, お前ら
demonstrative + ら: これら, それら, あれら
N(person) + ら: 子供ら, 学生ら, 田中さんら ('Tanaka and the others')
explanation: A plural suffix that is less polite than たち and much less polite than 方. With first-person pronouns it sounds casual or humble (僕ら), with second person it is rough (お前ら), and it should not be attached to people you need to respect. It is standard and neutral in 彼ら and in これら / それら, which are common in writing. In news style, 〜ら after a name means 'and others'.

examples.ja: 彼らは毎日遅くまで図書館で勉強している。
examples.en: They study in the library until late every day.

examples.ja: これらの問題について、もう少し考えてみましょう。
examples.en: Let's think a little more about these problems.

examples.ja: 僕らの学校には制服がない。
examples.en: Our school has no uniform.

match: (彼|彼女|僕|ぼく|俺|おれ|私|我|お前|君|子供|こども|あいつ|こいつ|これ|それ|あれ)ら(は|が|の|を|に|と|も|で|、)

meaning: whereas ~; in contrast to ~; while ~
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + の + に対して
Na + な + の + に対して / N + な / である + の + に対して
N + に対して (N as the item being contrasted)
S1。それに対して、S2。
explanation: Puts two things in sharp contrast on the same point: A is like this, whereas B is like that. A clause must be nominalized with の before に対して. It is objective and typical of written comparison. The same form after a plain noun can also mean 'toward, regarding' (先生に対して失礼だ); the contrast reading is the one where two parallel statements are being compared. 一方 is looser and can also present two sides of one thing.

examples.ja: 兄が静かなのに対して、弟はとてもにぎやかだ。
examples.en: Whereas the older brother is quiet, the younger brother is very lively.

examples.ja: 日本の大学は入るのが難しいのに対して、アメリカの大学は卒業するのが難しいと言われる。
examples.en: It is said that while Japanese universities are hard to get into, American universities are hard to graduate from.

examples.ja: 去年は雨が多かったのに対して、今年はほとんど降らない。
examples.en: In contrast to last year, when there was a lot of rain, it has hardly rained this year.

meaning: as long as ~; as far as ~; unless (with ない)
formation: V(dictionary / ている / ない-form) + 限り
A(い) + 限り / Na + な + 限り
N + である + 限り
V(dictionary / ている / た) + 限り(では) ('as far as I know / saw')
explanation: Sets a condition or limit and says the main clause holds for the whole time or range within it. With an ongoing state it means 'as long as'; with ない it means 'unless'; with verbs of knowing, seeing or checking plus では it means 'as far as'. Unlike たら or ば, it stresses that the result lasts exactly while the condition lasts. Fixed phrases include できる限り ('as much as possible').

examples.ja: 学生である限り、学校の規則は守らなければならない。
examples.en: As long as you are a student, you must follow the school rules.

examples.ja: 練習しない限り、上手にはならないよ。
examples.en: Unless you practice, you won't get good at it.

examples.ja: 私の知っている限りでは、彼は結婚していません。
examples.en: As far as I know, he is not married.

meaning: despite ~; in spite of ~; although ~
formation: N + にもかかわらず
V / A(い) (plain) + にもかかわらず
Na / N + (である) + にもかかわらず
S1。にもかかわらず / それにもかかわらず、S2。
explanation: A formal 'in spite of' that presents a fact and then a result contrary to what that fact would lead you to expect. It appears in writing, speeches and polite set phrases (お忙しいにもかかわらず). It carries surprise, criticism or appreciation depending on context. のに is the everyday equivalent and is more emotional; にもかかわらず is objective and cannot be followed by commands or requests.

examples.ja: 大雨にもかかわらず、たくさんの人が集まった。
examples.en: Despite the heavy rain, a lot of people gathered.

examples.ja: 何度も注意したにもかかわらず、彼はまた遅刻した。
examples.en: Even though I warned him many times, he was late again.

examples.ja: 忙しいにもかかわらず、手伝ってくださってありがとうございます。
examples.en: Thank you for helping me in spite of being busy.

match: にも(かかわ|関わ|拘わ|拘)らず

meaning: with much trouble; specially; (this) precious / rare ~
formation: せっかく + V(plain) + のに (regret that the effort or chance was wasted)
せっかく + V(plain) + (のだ)から (so let's make the most of it)
せっかくの + N
せっかくですが / せっかくだけど (polite refusal)
explanation: Shows that the speaker values an effort made or an opportunity that does not come often. With のに it expresses regret that this value was wasted; with から it urges making full use of it. せっかくの休み is 'a long-awaited day off'. せっかくですが softens a refusal of someone's kind offer. わざわざ focuses on going out of one's way to do something, while せっかく focuses on the worth of the effort or chance.

examples.ja: せっかく料理を作ったのに、誰も食べてくれなかった。
examples.en: I went to the trouble of cooking, but nobody ate it.

examples.ja: せっかく日本に来たのだから、いろいろな所へ行ってみたい。
examples.en: Since I've come all the way to Japan, I want to visit all sorts of places.

examples.ja: せっかくの休みなのに、一日中雨だった。
examples.en: It was my precious day off, and yet it rained all day.

meaning: even though I say ~; ~, but it's not as much as that sounds
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + と言っても / って言っても
Na / N (+ だ) + と言っても
S1。と言っても、S2。
explanation: Corrects the impression a word or statement might give by adding that the reality is more modest or limited than it sounds. The first part is admitted to be true, and the second part trims it down, often with だけ, しか or くらい. って言っても is the casual spoken form, and と言っても can start a new sentence. It is useful for speaking modestly about your own skills or circumstances.

examples.ja: 料理ができると言っても、簡単な物しか作れません。
examples.en: I say I can cook, but I can only make simple things.

examples.ja: 留学したって言っても、たった一か月だけだよ。
examples.en: I did say I studied abroad, but it was only for a month.

examples.ja: 社長と言っても、社員が三人の小さい会社です。
examples.en: I may be called company president, but it's a small company with three employees.

meaning: to the extent that ~; so ~ that ~; as ~ as ~
formation: V(plain, mostly dictionary / ない-form) + ほど + A / V
A(い) + ほど / N + ほど
〜ほどだ (sentence-final) / 〜ほどの + N
explanation: Describes how extreme a state is by naming something it is comparable to, often an exaggerated example: 'tired to the point of dying', 'so happy that tears come out'. It is like くらい in this use, but ほど tends to be chosen for the more extreme or figurative end and is slightly more formal. The clause before ほど is not something that literally happened; it is a yardstick. Do not confuse it with the negative comparison 〜ほど〜ない ('not as ~ as') or with 〜ば〜ほど.

examples.ja: 昨日は死ぬほど疲れた。
examples.en: Yesterday I was dead tired (tired to the point of dying).

examples.ja: この店は、並ばなければ入れないほど人気がある。
examples.en: This shop is so popular that you can't get in without lining up.

examples.ja: 涙が出るほどうれしかった。
examples.en: I was so happy I could have cried.

match: [うくぐすつぬぶむいた]ほど

meaning: it is said that ~; they say ~; reportedly ~
formation: S(plain) + という。
S(plain) + ということだ。/ とのことだ。
explanation: At the end of a sentence in written Japanese, という reports information that the writer got from elsewhere, without naming the source. It is the written counterpart of spoken 〜そうだ or 〜らしい and is common in newspaper articles, essays and stories about the past. It is normally written in kana and stays in the non-past form even when the content is past. Do not confuse it with N1 という N2 ('N2 called N1') in the middle of a sentence.

examples.ja: この寺は千年以上前に建てられたという。
examples.en: It is said that this temple was built more than a thousand years ago.

examples.ja: 日本には五万軒以上のコンビニがあるという。
examples.en: They say there are more than fifty thousand convenience stores in Japan.

examples.ja: 昔、この辺りは海だったという。
examples.en: Reportedly, this area used to be sea long ago.

meaning: in accordance with ~; to match ~; in time with ~
formation: N + に合わせて + V
N1 + を + N2 + に合わせる
N1 + に合わせた + N2
explanation: From the transitive verb 合わせる, 'to make something fit'. It says that someone adjusts an action or thing so that it suits a standard such as another person's needs, the season, a schedule or a rhythm. The adjustment is deliberate, which separates it from intransitive 合う ('to fit, to suit' as a state). 〜に応じて is a more formal near-synonym used when the response varies case by case.

examples.ja: 音楽に合わせて踊りましょう。
examples.en: Let's dance in time with the music.

examples.ja: 客の希望に合わせて、メニューを変えることができます。
examples.en: We can change the menu to match the customer's wishes.

examples.ja: この店は季節に合わせて商品を入れ替えている。
examples.en: This store changes its merchandise according to the season.

match: に(合|あ)わせ(て|る|た|、|ない|ます)

meaning: N2 that suits / fits / matches N1
formation: N1 + に合った + N2
N1 + に合う + N2
N2 + は + N1 + に合う / 合っている / 合わない
explanation: Uses intransitive 合う to say that something is a good fit for a person, purpose, level or condition. Before a noun, the た-form (合った) is preferred because it describes a resulting state, like 似た or 困った. The thing fitted to takes に. For clothes and colours looking good on someone, 似合う is the usual verb; 合う is about fit, compatibility and suitability. Compare 合わせる, where someone actively adjusts.

examples.ja: 自分に合った仕事を見つけるのは簡単ではない。
examples.en: Finding a job that suits you is not easy.

examples.ja: この辞書は初級の学生のレベルに合った説明が多い。
examples.en: This dictionary has many explanations suited to the level of beginning students.

examples.ja: 日本の気候に合った家を建てたい。
examples.en: I want to build a house that fits Japan's climate.

pattern: まるで〜(かの)ようだ / まるで〜みたいだ
romaji: marude you da / marude mitai da
meaning: just like ~; as if ~; as though ~
formation: まるで + N + の + ようだ / ように + V / ような + N
まるで + V(plain) + (かの)ようだ
まるで + N / V(plain) + みたいだ (casual)
explanation: まるで strengthens a simile, making clear that ようだ / みたいだ is a figurative comparison ('exactly as if') and not a conjecture ('it seems'). What follows is known not to be literally true. かのようだ after a verb is a more literary variant. In speech みたい replaces よう. Without まるで, the same sentence could be read as a guess about reality, so the adverb is a useful signal.

examples.ja: 彼女はまるで日本人のように日本語を話す。
examples.en: She speaks Japanese just like a Japanese person.

examples.ja: 今日は暖かくて、まるで春が来たようだ。
examples.en: It's so warm today, it's as if spring has come.

examples.ja: この店はまるで自分の家にいるみたいに落ち着く。
examples.en: This shop is so relaxing it's just like being in my own home.

pattern: 言うまでもない / 言うまでもなく
romaji: iu made mo nai / iu made mo naku
meaning: needless to say; it goes without saying
formation: S(plain) + の / こと + は言うまでもない
N + は言うまでもない
言うまでもなく、S
N1 + は言うまでもなく、N2 + も ('not to mention N1, N2 too')
explanation: States that something is so obvious that it hardly needs to be mentioned. It is built from V(dictionary) + までもない ('there is no need to go as far as ~'). As a sentence opener, 言うまでもなく works like 'of course'. In the pattern AはいうまでもなくBも, A is the obvious case and B the additional one. It is fairly formal; もちろん is the everyday equivalent.

examples.ja: 健康が何より大切なのは言うまでもない。
examples.en: It goes without saying that health is more important than anything.

examples.ja: 言うまでもなく、外国語の勉強には時間がかかる。
examples.en: Needless to say, studying a foreign language takes time.

examples.ja: 東京は言うまでもなく、地方の町でもコンビニはどこにでもある。
examples.en: Not to mention Tokyo, even in provincial towns convenience stores are everywhere.

meaning: even ~; as far as ~ (beyond what you'd expect)
formation: N + まで(も) (+ が / を may follow or be dropped)
N + に / と / で + まで
V(て-form) + まで ('go so far as to')
explanation: Beyond its basic sense of 'up to', まで can mark an item that lies at the far end of a range, showing surprise that things extend that far: 'not just the usual items, but even this'. Adding も strengthens the feeling. さえ picks a minimal example to imply the rest (often in negatives), while まで emphasizes that the scope has spread to an unexpected extreme, usually in affirmative sentences. Context tells it apart from the time and place limit 'until, as far as'.

examples.ja: 最近はコンビニで野菜までも買えるようになった。
examples.en: These days you can even buy vegetables at a convenience store.

examples.ja: 彼は親友にまでうそをついた。
examples.en: He lied even to his best friend.

examples.ja: 子供までがスマートフォンを持つ時代になった。
examples.en: We now live in a time when even children have smartphones.

meaning: whether X or Y; X, Y, or anything; be it X or Y
formation: N1 + でも + N2 + でも (+ predicate that applies to all)
N1 + でも + N2 + でも + いい ('either X or Y is fine')
explanation: Gives two or more examples and says the statement applies equally to each, and by implication to other things of the same kind. It is the noun version of 〜ても〜ても. The examples are samples, not a complete list, so the feeling is 'no matter which'. It differs from N1 も N2 も, which simply says 'both X and Y', by suggesting free choice or lack of restriction.

examples.ja: コンビニでは、弁当でも雑誌でも、ほしい物がすぐ買える。
examples.en: At a convenience store, whether it's a boxed lunch or a magazine, you can buy what you want right away.

examples.ja: 肉でも魚でも、好きなほうを選んでください。
examples.en: Meat or fish, please choose whichever you like.

examples.ja: 電話でもメールでもいいから、連絡してね。
examples.en: Either a call or an email is fine, so get in touch, OK?

meaning: therefore; consequently; accordingly
formation: S1。したがって、S2。
explanation: A formal connector that presents the second sentence as the logical consequence of the first. It belongs to academic writing, reports, legal and business language and formal speeches; in conversation だから or それで is used instead. The conclusion is a reasoned judgment or necessary result, so it is not used for commands or emotional reactions. Do not confuse it with N に従って ('in accordance with; as ~ changes').

examples.ja: この道は工事中である。したがって、車は通れない。
examples.en: This road is under construction. Therefore, cars cannot pass.

examples.ja: 参加者が少なかった。したがって、今回の旅行は中止する。
examples.en: There were few participants. Consequently, this trip will be cancelled.

examples.ja: 日本は資源が少ない。従って、多くの原料を輸入している。
examples.en: Japan has few resources. Accordingly, it imports many raw materials.

meaning: it is a fact that ~; it is true that ~
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + (という)のは事実だ
Na + な / N + だという + のは事実だ
〜のは事実だが、〜 (concession)
explanation: Affirms that something is objectively true. In argumentative writing it is most often used to concede a point before making a counter-argument: 〜のは事実だが、〜. こと can replace の (〜ことは事実だ). 確かに〜 gives a similar concession more casually. Adding という before の is common when the content is a general claim, and is required in practice after N + だ.

examples.ja: コンビニが私たちの生活を便利にしたのは事実だ。
examples.en: It is a fact that convenience stores have made our lives more convenient.

examples.ja: 彼が努力したというのは事実だが、結果は出なかった。
examples.en: It is true that he made an effort, but no results came of it.

examples.ja: この町に若い人が少なくなっているのは事実です。
examples.en: It is a fact that there are fewer and fewer young people in this town.

match: (の|こと)は事実(だ|です|である|で)

pattern: Nという点から考えると
romaji: to iu ten kara kangaeru to
meaning: considering it from the standpoint of N; in terms of N
formation: N + という点から考えると / 考えれば / 考えて
N + という点から見ると / 言うと
N + の点から(考えて)
explanation: Announces the angle from which a judgment is being made, so the conclusion that follows is understood to be valid for that criterion only. It lets a writer evaluate one topic from several angles in turn (price, safety, convenience). The verb can be 考える, 見る or 言う with little change in meaning. Shorter relatives are 〜の面では and 〜から言うと; 〜にとって is different because it gives a person's viewpoint, not a criterion.

examples.ja: 便利さという点から考えると、コンビニはスーパーよりいい。
examples.en: Considered from the standpoint of convenience, convenience stores are better than supermarkets.

examples.ja: 安全という点から考えると、この計画には問題がある。
examples.en: In terms of safety, this plan has problems.

examples.ja: 環境という点から見ると、車より電車のほうがいい。
examples.en: Looked at from the point of view of the environment, trains are better than cars.

match: (という|の)点から(考|見|言|い|み)

meaning: on top of ~; not only ~ but also; besides ~
formation: V / A(い) (plain) + 上(に)
Na + な + 上(に)
N + の / である + 上(に)
explanation: Stacks a second point on a first one that is evaluated the same way: both good or both bad. It emphasizes that the first fact alone would have been enough and the second makes it even more so. The main clause is a statement of fact, not a command or invitation. Sentence-initial その上 does the same job across two sentences. Do not confuse it with 〜上で ('after doing ~; in the process of ~') or with literal N の上に ('on top of N').

examples.ja: この店は安い上に、味もいい。
examples.en: This restaurant is cheap, and on top of that the food tastes good.

examples.ja: 昨日は財布をなくした上に、雨にも降られた。
examples.en: Yesterday I lost my wallet and, to make matters worse, got caught in the rain.

examples.ja: 彼は頭がいい上にスポーツもできる。
examples.en: Besides being smart, he is also good at sports.

meaning: to my (surprise / delight / regret), ~
formation: A(い) + ことに、S
Na + な + ことに、S
V(た-form) + ことに、S (驚いた / 困った / あきれた)
explanation: Places the speaker's emotional reaction first and then states the fact that caused it. Only a limited set of emotion words is used: うれしい, 残念な, 驚いた, 困った, 不思議な, ありがたい, 悲しい and the like. は may be added (驚いたことには). The main clause is an established fact, not a wish, intention or command. This is a written, slightly literary structure; in speech you would say the fact first and the feeling after.

examples.ja: 驚いたことに、彼は十か国語が話せるそうだ。
examples.en: To my surprise, I hear he can speak ten languages.

examples.ja: 残念なことに、楽しみにしていたコンサートが中止になった。
examples.en: Regrettably, the concert I had been looking forward to was cancelled.

examples.ja: うれしいことに、来月から給料が上がる。
examples.en: Happily, my salary goes up from next month.

meaning: but; however (written, plain style)
formation: S1。だが、S2。
explanation: A sentence-initial 'but' used in plain-style writing such as essays, articles and novels, where it matches the である / だ style. The polite counterpart is ですが, and the conversational ones are でも and けど. しかし is equally formal but neutral in tone and usable in polite speech; だが sounds firm and, when spoken, masculine or blunt. It is different from the clause-final copula + が in 学生だが.

examples.ja: コンビニは便利だ。だが、値段は少し高い。
examples.en: Convenience stores are convenient. But their prices are a little high.

examples.ja: 彼は一生懸命頑張った。だが、試験には合格できなかった。
examples.en: He tried his very best. However, he could not pass the exam.

examples.ja: 計画はよくできている。だが、問題はお金だ。
examples.en: The plan is well made. But the problem is money.

pattern: Nに対して / N1に対するN2
meaning: toward ~; to ~; regarding ~; against ~
formation: N + に対して + V / A
N1 + に対する + N2
N1 + に対しての + N2
explanation: Marks the person or thing that an attitude, feeling, action or response is directed at: being kind to someone, objecting to an opinion, answering a question, interest in a field. It is more formal and explicit than plain に. Before a noun, use に対する. について introduces the topic that is talked or thought about, whereas に対して marks a target that is faced or acted upon. The same form can also express contrast ('whereas'), usually after の.

examples.ja: 店員は客に対して丁寧な言葉を使わなければならない。
examples.en: Shop staff must use polite language toward customers.

examples.ja: コンビニの深夜営業に対する批判が増えている。
examples.en: Criticism of convenience stores' late-night opening is increasing.

examples.ja: 先生は学生の質問に対して、一つ一つ丁寧に答えた。
examples.en: The teacher answered the students' questions carefully, one by one.

match: [^のれ]に(対|たい)(して|する|し、|しまして)

meaning: there is no need to ~; you don't have to ~
formation: V(dictionary) + ことはない
何も / わざわざ / そんなに + V(dictionary) + ことはない
explanation: Tells someone that an action is unnecessary, usually to reassure or advise them, and sometimes to criticize an over-reaction. It is close to 〜なくてもいい and 〜必要はない but is more personal and encouraging. It is said about the listener or a third person, not normally about yourself. Watch the verb form: V(た) + ことはない means 'have never done', and V(ない) + ことはない is a double negative meaning 'it's not that I don't'.

examples.ja: 時間は十分あるから、急ぐことはないよ。
examples.en: We have plenty of time, so there's no need to hurry.

examples.ja: 電話で話せば済むことだから、わざわざ行くことはない。
examples.en: It can be settled by phone, so there is no need to go all the way there.

examples.ja: 一度失敗したぐらいで、そんなに心配することはありません。
examples.en: You don't need to worry that much just because you failed once.

match: (る|う|く|ぐ|す|つ|ぬ|ぶ|む)(こと|事)は(ない|ありません)

romaji: ka to iu to / ka to ieba
meaning: if you ask whether / why ~; you might think ~, but
formation: question word + S(plain) + かというと、〜 (からだ)
S(plain) + かというと、(そうでもない / そうとは限らない)
〜かと言えば / 〜かって言うと (variants)
explanation: Poses a question yourself and then answers it, a common way to structure explanations. With a question word (なぜ, どうして, 何) it sets up the answer, which often ends in からだ. Without one, it raises an assumption the listener might hold and then denies or qualifies it ('you would think so, but not really'). Na and N usually drop だ before か. It gives the listener a moment to anticipate the point.

examples.ja: なぜコンビニが人気があるかというと、いつでも開いているからだ。
examples.en: The reason convenience stores are popular is that they are always open.

examples.ja: 日本料理が全部好きかというと、そうでもない。
examples.en: If you ask whether I like all Japanese food, not really.

examples.ja: どうして遅れたかと言うと、電車が止まっていたんです。
examples.en: As for why I was late, the trains had stopped.

meaning: in that case; if so; then
formation: A: S1。 B: それなら、S2。
それなら / そんなら (casual) / それでしたら (polite)
explanation: Takes what the other person has just said as a condition and gives the speaker's response to it: a suggestion, a decision, a conclusion or a request. It is mostly used across turns in a dialogue. では and じゃ are broader 'well then' markers; それなら insists on the if-that-is-the-case logic, like the conditional なら. すると, in contrast, draws a factual inference and is not followed by suggestions or intentions.

examples.ja: 「今日は車で来ました。」「それなら、お酒は飲めませんね。」
examples.en: "I came by car today." "In that case, you can't drink, can you?"

examples.ja: 「この店は九時に閉まるそうだよ。」「それなら、急いで行こう。」
examples.en: "I hear this shop closes at nine." "Then let's hurry and go."

examples.ja: 「一人で行くのは不安なんです。」「それなら、私も一緒に行きましょう。」
examples.en: "I'm nervous about going alone." "In that case, I'll go with you."

match: それなら|そんなら|それでしたら

meaning: there are quite a few; not uncommon; many
formation: N + は/が/も + 少なくない
S(plain) + N(人/こと/場合 etc.) + は/も + 少なくない
explanation: Literally "is not few": an understatement that actually means "there are a good many". It belongs mainly to written or formal Japanese and is used as a predicate at the end of the clause. It does not modify a noun directly (×少なくない人が来た); put the noun first and finish with 少なくない, or use 多くの N instead. The polite form is 少なくありません.

examples.ja: この町には、江戸時代の建物が今も残っている所が少なくない。
examples.en: In this town there are quite a few places where Edo-period buildings still remain.

examples.ja: 歴史に興味を持つ留学生も少なくない。
examples.en: International students who take an interest in history are not few either.

examples.ja: 便利になった一方で、昔のほうがよかったと言う人も少なくありません。
examples.en: While things have become convenient, quite a lot of people say the old days were better.

match: 少なく(は)?(ない|ありません|なかった)
すくなく(は)?(ない|ありません)

pattern: N を通して / N を通じて
meaning: through; via; by way of; throughout (a period)
formation: N(medium / person / experience) + を通して
N(period) + を通して (throughout N)
N + を通じて (slightly more formal)
explanation: Marks the medium, go-between or experience by way of which something is done, learned or obtained. With a period of time (一年を通して) it means "all through". Plain で also marks a means, but を通して stresses that something passes via an intermediary rather than being done directly. Do not confuse it with を通る, "to pass through a place".

examples.ja: 留学生活を通して、日本の文化だけでなく自分の国のこともよく分かるようになった。
examples.en: Through my life as an exchange student, I came to understand not only Japanese culture but my own country as well.

examples.ja: 友達を通して、今のルームメイトと知り合いました。
examples.en: I got to know my current roommate through a friend.

examples.ja: この地方は一年を通して雨が多い。
examples.en: This region gets a lot of rain throughout the year.

pattern: N1 から N2 にかけて
meaning: from X through Y; over the span from X to Y (loose range)
formation: N1(time/place) + から + N2(time/place) + にかけて
N1 + から + N2 + にかけての + N
explanation: Gives a rough span of time or space within which something happens. Unlike から〜まで, the start and end points are vague and the event need not continue across the entire range; it only has to occur somewhere over it. You hear it constantly in weather reports and read it in history writing. For exact limits (9時から5時まで働く) use から〜まで instead.

examples.ja: 今晩から明日の朝にかけて、強い雨が降るでしょう。
examples.en: Heavy rain is expected from tonight through tomorrow morning.

examples.ja: 十六世紀から十七世紀にかけて、多くのヨーロッパ人が日本を訪れた。
examples.en: From the 16th into the 17th century, many Europeans visited Japan.

examples.ja: 関東から東北にかけての地域で地震があった。
examples.en: There was an earthquake in the area stretching from Kanto to Tohoku.

pattern: N で言うと / N で言えば
meaning: in terms of X; expressed in X; if we put it in X
formation: N + で言うと
N + で言えば / で言ったら
explanation: Names the scale, system or frame of reference into which you are converting or restating something: a calendar system, a unit, a familiar comparison. It helps the listener picture the thing in terms they know. It is not a source marker; "according to (someone)" is によると.

examples.ja: 1868年は、日本の年号で言うと明治元年です。
examples.en: The year 1868 is, in terms of Japanese era names, the first year of Meiji.

examples.ja: この大学の学生数は、日本の大学で言うと中ぐらいの大きさだ。
examples.en: In terms of Japanese universities, this school's enrollment is about medium size.

examples.ja: 彼女の日本語は、レベルで言えば上級に近い。
examples.en: Her Japanese is, level-wise, close to advanced.

match: で(言|い)(うと|えば|ったら)

meaning: each; every; the various ~
formation: 各 + N (mostly kanji compounds: 各国, 各地, 各自, 各家庭; also 各クラス, 各チーム)
explanation: A formal prefix that views the members of a group one by one: 各国 "each country / the various countries". It is common in announcements, news and written explanations; in conversation それぞれの N sounds softer. Do not use it for repetition in time; that is 毎 (毎週, 毎年). 各 is read かく.

examples.ja: サミットには世界各国の代表が集まった。
examples.en: Representatives of countries from around the world gathered at the summit.

examples.ja: 各クラスから二人ずつ代表を選んでください。
examples.en: Please choose two representatives from each class.

examples.ja: 祭りは日本各地で行われている。
examples.en: Festivals are held in every part of Japan.

pattern: X ばかりで(は)なく Y(も)
meaning: not only X but also Y
formation: N + ばかりで(は)なく + N + も
V / A-い (plain) + ばかりで(は)なく
Na + な + ばかりで(は)なく
explanation: Adds Y on top of X: "X, and what is more, Y". It means the same as だけでなく but sounds a little more formal and written; ばかりか is stronger still. Y is usually marked with も or まで. Keep it apart from the other ばかり patterns: V-たばかり (just did) and V-てばかりいる (do nothing but).

examples.ja: 漢字は日本ばかりでなく、中国や台湾でも使われている。
examples.en: Kanji are used not only in Japan but also in China and Taiwan.

examples.ja: 彼は歴史に詳しいばかりでなく、説明も上手だ。
examples.en: He not only knows a lot about history but is also good at explaining it.

examples.ja: この寺は古いばかりではなく、建物としても大変美しい。
examples.en: This temple is not merely old; it is also very beautiful as a building.

keywords: not only x but also y

meaning: -style; in the manner of; looking like
formation: N + 風 + の + N
N + 風 + に + V
N + 風 + だ
explanation: A suffix (read ふう) that says something has the style, flavor or outward look of N: 和風 Japanese-style, 洋風 Western-style, 学生風 student-looking. It often implies "in that style" rather than the genuine article. Compare 〜っぽい (casual "-ish", a tendency) and 〜式 (a system or method, 日本式). こういう風に "in this way" uses the same word.

examples.ja: 駅前に和風のレストランができた。
examples.en: A Japanese-style restaurant opened in front of the station.

examples.ja: この料理は、ヨーロッパ風に味をつけてあります。
examples.en: This dish has been seasoned in a European style.

examples.ja: サラリーマン風の男の人が道を聞いてきた。
examples.en: A man who looked like an office worker asked me for directions.

match: (日本|中国|韓国|西洋|東洋|現代|昔|学生|関西|関東|京都|田舎)風

pattern: N と共に / V と共に
meaning: together with; along with; as ~ (changes over time)
formation: N(person/organization) + と共に (together with)
N(change/time) + と共に (as N proceeds)
V(dictionary) + と共に (at the same time as / as)
explanation: A written-style expression with three uses: (1) "together with" someone, the formal partner of と一緒に; (2) "at the same time as"; (3) "as X changes, Y changes too" (時代と共に). と一緒に cannot express the third meaning. Do not mix it up with N1、N2共に "both N1 and N2", where no と appears.

examples.ja: 家族と共に日本へ移り住んだ。
examples.en: He moved to Japan together with his family.

examples.ja: 時代と共に、人々の考え方も変わってきた。
