examples.en: With the times, people's ways of thinking have changed as well.

examples.ja: 年を取ると共に、歴史への興味が強くなった。
examples.en: As I got older, my interest in history grew stronger.

meaning: each; apiece; (a little) at a time; by (twos, etc.)
formation: Number + counter + ずつ
少し / ちょっと / いくらか + ずつ
explanation: Attaches to a quantity to show that the same amount goes to each member or is repeated each time: 一人ずつ "one person at a time", 少しずつ "little by little". It follows the quantity word, never a bare noun (×学生ずつ). Compare 〜ごとに, which attaches to the unit over which something repeats (三日ごとに "every three days").

examples.ja: 一人に二枚ずつ紙を配ってください。
examples.en: Please hand out two sheets of paper to each person.

examples.ja: 毎日少しずつ漢字を覚えています。
examples.en: I am memorizing kanji a little at a time every day.

examples.ja: 子供たちは一人ずつ名前を呼ばれた。
examples.en: The children had their names called one by one.

pattern: N1 から N2 に至るまで
meaning: from X all the way to Y; everything from X to Y
formation: N1 + から + N2 + に至るまで
explanation: An emphatic, formal version of から〜まで that stresses how wide the range is, with N2 as a far or surprising end point. It often lists two extremes to mean "everything and everyone in between". Use plain から〜まで for neutral ranges, and から〜にかけて for a loose span in which something happens.

examples.ja: この店には、野菜から家具に至るまで何でもそろっている。
examples.en: This store has everything, from vegetables all the way to furniture.

examples.ja: 子供から老人に至るまで、町中の人が祭りに参加した。
examples.en: From children to the elderly, the whole town took part in the festival.

examples.ja: 江戸時代には、武士から農民に至るまで、身分によって生活が決められていた。
examples.en: In the Edo period, life was determined by social status for everyone from samurai down to farmers.

meaning: fellow ~; among/between people (things) of the same kind
formation: N + 同士 + で / が / の
N + 同士 + だ
explanation: A suffix showing that the people or things named stand in the same relation to each other and do something mutually or among themselves: 友達同士 "as friends / between friends", 国同士 "between countries". It is not a general word for "each other"; that is お互い(に). It must follow a noun naming the category the members share.

examples.ja: 留学生同士で日本語で話すようにしている。

match: [一二三四五六七八九][、・][二三四五六七八九十](日|人|年|回|時間|分|個|本|枚|冊|度|週間|か月|ヶ月|歳|台|杯|軒|匹|倍|十|百|千|万)

meaning: as it is; left in the state of; still ~ (unchanged)
formation: V(た) + まま
V(ない) + まま
N + の + まま
A-い / Na-な + まま; この / その / あの + まま
explanation: Shows that a state stays unchanged while something else happens, often when a change would normally be expected. Use the た-form for a resulting state, never the dictionary form (×窓を開けるまま). ながら links two actions done at once, whereas まま is about an unchanged condition. 〜っぱなし is similar but casual and critical in tone.

examples.ja: 窓を開けたまま、出かけてしまった。
examples.en: I went out leaving the window open.

examples.ja: この町には、昔のままの古い家が残っている。
examples.en: In this town, old houses remain just as they were long ago.

examples.ja: 作り方が分からないまま、とにかく始めてみた。
examples.en: Without understanding how to make it, I just went ahead and started.

meaning: one's 20s, 30s...; the (19)60s; decade
formation: Number (multiple of ten) + 代 (十代, 二十代, 五十代)
Year + 年代 (1960年代)
〜代 + 前半 / 後半 / 半ば
explanation: Attached to a multiple of ten, 代 gives an age bracket (二十代 = ages 20-29; 十代 = teens), and 年代 gives a decade or era (1980年代 = the 1980s). Add 前半, 半ば or 後半 for "early, mid, late". Do not confuse it with 〜代 meaning "charge" (電気代), with 時代 "era", or with 世代 "generation".

examples.ja: 彼女は二十代で自分の会社を作った。
examples.en: She started her own company in her twenties.

examples.ja: 1960年代に、日本の経済は大きく成長した。
examples.en: In the 1960s, the Japanese economy grew dramatically.

examples.ja: この山には、六十代、七十代の人もたくさん登りに来る。
examples.en: Many people in their sixties and seventies also come to climb this mountain.

meaning: the figure / sight / appearance of ~ (doing)
formation: N + の + 姿
V(plain) + 姿
姿 + を見せる / が見える / を消す
explanation: 姿 is the visible form of a person or thing taken as a whole. With a verb clause in front (子供が遊ぶ姿) it presents someone caught in the act and is more vivid than V のを見る. Compare 形 (shape or outline), 様子 (condition or state, not only visual) and 格好 (outfit or posture). 姿を消す "to disappear" and 姿を見せる "to show up" are set phrases.

examples.ja: 子供たちが雪の中で遊ぶ姿を見て、うれしくなった。
examples.en: Seeing the children playing in the snow made me happy.

examples.ja: 着物を着た彼女の姿は、とても美しかった。
examples.en: The sight of her in a kimono was very beautiful.

examples.ja: 山の上から、雲の間に富士山の姿が見えた。
examples.en: From the mountaintop, the form of Mt. Fuji was visible between the clouds.

meaning: do X and then Y, over and over
formation: V1(て) + は + V2(ます-stem)、V1(て) + は + V2(ます-stem) + (する)
V1(て) + は + V2 (habitual pair)
explanation: Describes a pair of actions that repeats again and again: 書いては消し、書いては消し "writing and erasing, writing and erasing". The pair is often said twice, with V2 in the ます-stem. It has a descriptive, somewhat literary feel. This is not the conditional ては of 〜てはいけない or 〜ては困る, which means "if".

examples.ja: 雨が降ってはやみ、降ってはやみして、一日中はっきりしない天気だった。
examples.en: The rain kept starting and stopping, and the weather stayed unsettled all day.

examples.ja: 手紙を書いては消し、書いては消しして、やっと書き終えた。
examples.en: I wrote and erased the letter over and over, and finally finished it.

examples.ja: 休みの日は、食べては寝るだけの生活をしている。
examples.en: On my days off, all I do is eat and sleep, over and over.

meaning: used to ~; would often ~ (fond recollection)
formation: V(た) + ものだ / ものです
(よく) + V(た) + もんだ (casual)
explanation: Looks back with feeling on something one did habitually in the past; it often comes with よく, 昔は or 子供のころ. It is not used for one-time events. Plain 〜ていた states the past habit neutrally, while 〜たものだ adds nostalgia. Do not confuse it with V-る ものだ, which states how things generally are or should be.

examples.ja: 子供のころは、よく近くの川で泳いだものだ。
examples.en: When I was a child, I often used to swim in the nearby river.

examples.ja: 学生時代は、朝まで友達と話したものです。
examples.en: In my student days, I would talk with friends until morning.

examples.ja: 昔は、この辺りでもホタルが見られたものだ。
examples.en: In the old days, you used to be able to see fireflies around here too.

meaning: gradually; little by little; more and more
formation: だんだん + A-くなる / Na-になる / V(change)
だんだん(と) + V-てくる / V-ていく
explanation: Shows that a change advances step by step, so it combines with expressions of change such as 〜くなる, 〜てくる and 〜ていく. どんどん suggests a rapid, unstoppable pace; 少しずつ focuses on small amounts; ますます means "even more" on top of an already high degree. だんだん is neutral and works in both speech and writing.

examples.ja: 三月になって、だんだん暖かくなってきた。
examples.en: March has come, and it has gradually been getting warmer.

examples.ja: 日本語の授業がだんだん難しくなっていく。
examples.en: The Japanese class keeps getting gradually harder.

examples.ja: 空がだんだんと明るくなり、鳥が鳴き始めた。
examples.en: The sky grew lighter little by little, and the birds began to sing.

meaning: as ~ (changes), ~ (changes with it)
formation: V(dictionary; verb of change) + につれて
N(noun of change) + につれて
explanation: Links two gradual changes: as the first proceeds, the second follows in proportion. Both clauses must describe change, and the second clause cannot be a command, request or one-time intention. に従って is similar but can also mean "in obedience to" and allows intentional actions; と共に stresses that the two happen together.

examples.ja: 秋が深まるにつれて、山の木々が赤や黄色に変わっていく。
examples.en: As autumn deepens, the trees on the mountains turn red and yellow.

examples.ja: 年を取るにつれて、季節の変化を楽しめるようになった。
examples.en: As I have grown older, I have come to enjoy the changing of the seasons.

examples.ja: 町の発展につれて、自然が少なくなってきた。
examples.en: With the development of the town, nature has been disappearing.

pattern: V(ます-stem) + 上げる / 上がる
meaning: finish ~ing; complete; ~ up
formation: V(ます-stem) + 上げる (transitive: 書き上げる, 作り上げる, 仕上げる)
V(ます-stem) + 上がる (intransitive: でき上がる, 仕上がる)
explanation: As a compound-verb ending, 上げる shows that something is brought to completion through effort, usually with a finished product as the result (書き上げる "finish writing"). It can also keep its literal sense of upward motion (持ち上げる, 見上げる). 〜終わる only says the action ends, and 〜切る stresses using up or going all the way. Only certain verbs take it.

examples.ja: 彼は三年かけて、長い小説を書き上げた。
examples.en: He spent three years and finished writing a long novel.

examples.ja: 一晩でレポートを仕上げなければならない。
examples.en: I have to get the report finished in one night.

examples.ja: 子供たちは力を合わせて、大きな雪だるまを作り上げた。
examples.en: The children worked together and built up a big snowman.

match: [一-龥][いきぎしちにびみりえけげせてねべめれ]?上げ(る|た|て|ま|な|ら|れ|よ)

meaning: on the way (out / back); just as one is ~ing
formation: V(ます-stem) + がけ + に (帰りがけに, 行きがけに, 出がけに, 通りがけに)
V(ます-stem) + がけ + の + N
explanation: Used with a small set of motion verbs to say that something is done or happens on the occasion of that movement, either in the middle of it or just as it begins: 帰りがけに "on my way home". It is narrower than 途中で, and unlike ついでに it does not stress taking advantage of an opportunity. Do not confuse it with 〜かけ "half-done" (食べかけ).

examples.ja: 帰りがけに、スーパーで牛乳を買った。
examples.en: On my way home, I bought milk at the supermarket.

examples.ja: 出がけに電話がかかってきて、遅れてしまった。
examples.en: A phone call came just as I was leaving, and I ended up late.

examples.ja: 行きがけに、この手紙をポストに入れてくれませんか。
examples.en: Could you drop this letter in the mailbox on your way there?

match: (帰り|行き|出|通り|来|寝|起き)がけ

meaning: just by ~ing; ~ alone is enough to
formation: V(plain) + だけで
N + だけで
A-い / Na-な + だけで
explanation: Says that a minimal thing is all it takes to bring about the result: 見るだけで分かる "you can tell just by looking", 考えただけで "at the mere thought". The result follows naturally, so it is often a feeling or an automatic reaction. Do not confuse it with 〜だけでなく "not only", or with the limiting use "with only" (水だけで生きる).

examples.ja: この写真を見るだけで、故郷の秋を思い出す。
examples.en: Just looking at this photo reminds me of autumn in my hometown.

examples.ja: 試験のことを考えただけで、おなかが痛くなる。
examples.en: Just thinking about the exam gives me a stomachache.

examples.ja: 桜の花が咲くだけで、町全体が明るくなったように感じる。
examples.en: The cherry blossoms coming out is enough to make the whole town feel brighter.

pattern: あまりに(も) / あまりの N に
romaji: amari ni (mo) / amari no N ni
meaning: too; excessively; so ~ (that)
formation: あまりに(も) + A / Na / V
あまりに(も) + A-くて / Na-で / 〜ので、…
あまりの + N(often A-さ) + に、…
explanation: Marks a degree far beyond what is normal, usually leading to a consequence: "so beautiful that I was speechless". It is used in affirmative statements; this is the opposite of あまり〜ない "not very". It frequently teams up with 〜すぎる (あまりにも高すぎる), and あんまり is the casual form. あまりの N に takes a noun, often an adjective turned into a noun with さ.

examples.ja: 景色があまりにも美しくて、言葉が出なかった。
examples.en: The scenery was so beautiful that I was at a loss for words.

examples.ja: この俳句はあまりに有名なので、知らない日本人はいないだろう。
examples.en: This haiku is so famous that there is probably no Japanese person who does not know it.

examples.ja: あまりの寒さに、外に出る気がしなかった。
examples.en: It was so cold that I did not feel like going outside.

meaning: in order to ~; for ~ing (what it takes)
formation: V(dictionary) + には + requirement / evaluation (〜が必要だ, 〜がいい, 〜なければならない)
N + には (for the purpose of N)
explanation: Takes a goal as the topic and then states what is needed, suitable or difficult for achieving it. Unlike ために, the main clause is a judgment or requirement, not an action the subject performs toward the goal: 行くには "if you want to go / for going". Do not confuse it with には after a place or person (日本には, 私には難しい).

examples.ja: 俳句を作るには、季語を知らなければならない。
examples.en: To compose haiku, you have to know the season words.

examples.ja: 富士山に登るには、夏が一番いい。
examples.en: For climbing Mt. Fuji, summer is best.

examples.ja: この川をきれいにするには、長い時間がかかるだろう。
examples.en: It will probably take a long time to make this river clean.

meaning: roughly; about; mostly; on the whole; (complaint) in the first place
formation: だいたい + number / quantity
だいたい + V / A (for the most part)
だいたいの + N
だいたい、S (in the first place; criticism)
explanation: Means "approximately" before numbers and "for the most part" before verbs and adjectives (だいたい分かった). At the head of a complaint it means "to begin with" (だいたい君は遅すぎる). ほとんど is closer to "nearly all", たいてい is about frequency ("usually"), and 約 is a formal "approximately" used only with numbers.

examples.ja: 駅からここまで、だいたい十五分ぐらいです。
examples.en: From the station to here it is roughly fifteen minutes.

examples.ja: 先生の説明はだいたい分かりました。
examples.en: I understood most of the teacher's explanation.

examples.ja: だいたいの人は、春になると花見に出かける。
examples.en: Most people go out to see the cherry blossoms when spring comes.

pattern: N における / N において
meaning: in; at; on (place, time, field) — formal
formation: N + において(は / も) + V
N + における + N
N + においての + N
explanation: The formal, written equivalent of で for the place, time or field in which something happens. において modifies a verb and における modifies a noun (= での). It appears in speeches, papers and official notices. It cannot replace で of means or material (バスで, 木で), and it is too stiff for everyday conversation.

examples.ja: 日本における自然と人間の関係について研究している。
examples.en: I am researching the relationship between nature and people in Japan.

examples.ja: 現代社会において、環境問題は最も重要な問題の一つである。
examples.en: In modern society, environmental issues are among the most important problems.

examples.ja: 卒業式は大学のホールにおいて行われます。
examples.en: The graduation ceremony will be held in the university hall.

meaning: also; too; as well (emphatic, reflective)
formation: N + もまた
N + particle + もまた
S(plain) + の / こと + もまた
explanation: も strengthened by また: "X, too, is ...". It has a written, thoughtful tone and is used when setting something beside what has just been mentioned and granting it equal standing. Do not confuse it with また alone ("again" or "furthermore") or with または ("or").

examples.ja: 春の桜は美しいが、秋の紅葉もまた美しい。
examples.en: The cherry blossoms of spring are beautiful, but the autumn leaves, too, are beautiful.

examples.ja: 自然を守ることもまた、私たちの大切な仕事である。
examples.en: Protecting nature is also an important task of ours.

examples.ja: 失敗もまた、いい経験になる。
examples.en: Failure, too, becomes good experience.

meaning: oh, (is that all); why, ...! (letdown or relief)
formation: なんだ、S(plain) (often + のか / じゃないか)
なあんだ (drawn out)
explanation: A casual interjection said on discovering that something is less serious, less impressive or simpler than expected, expressing mild disappointment or relief: "Oh, so that is all it was". It comes at the start of the sentence, often followed by 〜のか or 〜じゃないか. Distinguish it from the question 何だ "what is it?" and from explanatory 〜なんだ after a noun (学生なんだ).

examples.ja: なんだ、夢だったのか。
examples.en: Oh, so it was just a dream.

examples.ja: なんだ、まだだれも来ていないじゃないか。
examples.en: What, nobody has come yet!

examples.ja: なあんだ、そんなに簡単なことだったの。
examples.en: Oh, so it was something that simple?

meaning: come to ~; start to ~; have been ~ing (up to now)
formation: V(て) + くる
A-く / Na-に + なってくる
V(て) + きた (has come to / has been ~ing until now)
explanation: With verbs of change or perception, てくる shows that a change begins or gradually becomes noticeable to the speaker (暖かくなってくる, 雨が降ってきた), or that something has continued from the past up to the present (守ってきた). Its partner ていく looks from now into the future. The same form can also be literal: 買ってくる "go buy and come back".

examples.ja: 三月になると、少しずつ暖かくなってくる。
examples.en: When March comes, it starts getting warmer little by little.

examples.ja: 急に空が暗くなって、雨が降ってきた。
examples.en: The sky suddenly turned dark and it began to rain.

examples.ja: 日本人は昔から、季節の変化を大切にしてきた。
examples.en: Since long ago, the Japanese have valued the changing of the seasons.

meaning: except (for); excluding; with the exception of
formation: N + を除いて(は)
N + を除く + N
N + を除けば
explanation: Sets N aside as the exception to the statement that follows. It is more formal than 以外 and is common in notices, reports and news. N を除く N modifies a noun ("all members excluding the chair"). 以外 can also mean "other than / besides", while を除いて is strictly "leaving out".

examples.ja: 日曜日を除いて、毎日営業しています。
examples.en: We are open every day except Sunday.

examples.ja: 一部の地域を除いて、明日は全国的に晴れるでしょう。
examples.en: With the exception of some areas, it will be sunny nationwide tomorrow.

examples.ja: 首相を除く大臣全員が、その会議に出席した。
examples.en: All the ministers except the prime minister attended the meeting.

match: を(除|のぞ)(いて|く|けば|き)

meaning: that is (to say); namely; in other words
formation: X、すなわち Y
S1。すなわち、S2。
explanation: A formal connector that restates X as Y, where the two are exactly equivalent: a definition, a paraphrase or a precise identification. It belongs to written and lecture style. つまり is the everyday word and often sums up or draws a conclusion; すなわち simply says "which is to say".

examples.ja: 国会は二つの議院、すなわち衆議院と参議院からできている。
examples.en: The Diet is made up of two houses, namely the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors.

examples.ja: 日本の首都、すなわち東京には、政治の中心となる機関が集まっている。
examples.en: In the capital of Japan, that is to say Tokyo, the central institutions of politics are concentrated.

examples.ja: 選挙権は十八歳以上の国民、すなわち大人に与えられている。
examples.en: The right to vote is given to citizens aged eighteen and over, in other words adults.

meaning: for the time being; more or less; just in case; technically
formation: 一応 + V
一応 + N + だ / です
一応の + N
explanation: Says that something is done or holds in a provisional, minimal way rather than fully. Main uses: (1) "for now / roughly" (一応できた "it is done, more or less"); (2) "just in case" (一応確認する); (3) a modest hedge about oneself (一応、医者です "I am a doctor, technically"). とりあえず is about doing something first as a stopgap, and 念のため only means "to be on the safe side".

examples.ja: レポートは一応書き終わったが、もう一度見直すつもりだ。
examples.en: I have more or less finished writing the report, but I intend to look it over once more.

examples.ja: 大丈夫だと思いますが、一応確認しておきます。
examples.en: I think it is fine, but I will check just in case.

examples.ja: 一応、大学では政治学を専攻しました。
examples.en: For what it is worth, I majored in political science at university.

pattern: N を左右する / N に左右される
romaji: wo sayuu suru / ni sayuu sareru
meaning: to sway; to decide the fate of / to be at the mercy of
formation: N1 + が + N2 + を左右する
N2 + は / が + N1 + に左右される (passive)
explanation: Literally "to move left and right": one factor has the power to determine how something turns out. It is stronger than 影響を与える, which only says there is some effect. The passive 〜に左右される, "to be swayed by / dependent on", is especially common. It is a written-style expression used for outcomes, fates, prices and results.

examples.ja: 若い人たちの票が、選挙の結果を左右するだろう。
examples.en: The votes of young people will likely decide the outcome of the election.

examples.ja: 農業は天気に左右されやすい。
examples.en: Agriculture is easily affected by the weather.

examples.ja: この決定は、国の将来を左右する重要なものだ。
examples.en: This decision is an important one that will determine the future of the country.

meaning: both N1 and N2; ~ alike
formation: N1、N2 + 共に
N1 + も + N2 + も + 共に
N(pair or group: 男女, 両国, 両者) + 共に
explanation: Placed after two or more listed items, 共に says the statement applies equally to all of them: "both A and B". It is formal and compact, frequent in news and reports. Do not confuse it with N と共に ("together with N" or "as N changes"); here there is no と, and 共に refers back to the listed items.

examples.ja: 衆議院、参議院共に、議員は選挙で選ばれる。
examples.en: In both the House of Representatives and the House of Councillors, members are chosen by election.

examples.ja: この町は、人口、面積共に県内で一番小さい。
examples.en: This town is the smallest in the prefecture in both population and area.

examples.ja: 父も母も共に、その政党を支持している。
examples.en: Both my father and my mother support that party.

meaning: to enter (a period); once ~ begins; since ~ began
formation: N(period: 今月, 四月, 二十一世紀, 1990年代, 夏休み) + に入る
N + に入って(から)、…
N + に入ると、…
explanation: Treats a period of time as a space one moves into and marks its beginning: 今月に入ってから "since this month began". It is used with months, years, decades, eras, seasons and stages (後半に入る, 梅雨に入る), not with points in time (×三時に入る). Compare 〜になる, which just says a time arrives.

examples.ja: 今月に入ってから、雨の日が続いている。
examples.en: Since this month began, rainy days have continued.

examples.ja: 二十一世紀に入り、世界の政治は大きく変わった。
examples.en: With the start of the 21st century, world politics changed greatly.

examples.ja: 選挙戦は後半に入った。
examples.en: The election campaign has entered its second half.

match: (年|月|世紀|年代|時代|期|週|休み|半|梅雨|春|夏|秋|冬)に(入|はい)(る|り|って|った|ります|りました|ると|れば)

pattern: 〜を問題にする / 〜が問題になる
romaji: wo mondai ni suru / ga mondai ni naru
meaning: to make an issue of / to become an issue
formation: N / S(plain)+こと + を問題にする (someone takes it up as a problem)
N / S(plain)+こと + が問題になる (it becomes a problem)
N / S(plain)+こと + が問題にされる (passive)
explanation: The usual にする / になる pair applied to 問題. 〜を問題にする means someone actively raises something for criticism or discussion; 〜が問題になる means it turns into a matter of public concern on its own; 〜が問題にされる is the passive, "is called into question". Note the idiom 問題にならない, "to be out of the question / no match at all".

examples.ja: 野党は、大臣の発言を問題にしている。
examples.en: The opposition parties are making an issue of the minister's remarks.

examples.ja: 最近、若者の投票率の低さが問題になっている。
examples.en: Recently, low voter turnout among young people has become an issue.

examples.ja: 政治家とお金の関係が、国会で問題にされた。
examples.en: The relationship between politicians and money was called into question in the Diet.

match: 問題に(する|し|さ|なる|なり|なっ|なら)

meaning: still; even now (longer than one would expect)
formation: 未だに + V(ている / affirmative)
未だに + V(ない / ていない)
explanation: A stronger まだ: it stresses that a situation that should have changed long ago still has not, with a tone of surprise or criticism. It is used with both affirmative and negative predicates and is often written in kana (いまだに). 今でも also means "even now" but is neutral and suits fond memories; 未だに hints that something is overdue.

examples.ja: あの事件の原因は、未だに分かっていない。
examples.en: The cause of that incident is still unknown even now.

examples.ja: 祖父は未だに携帯電話を使おうとしない。
examples.en: My grandfather still refuses to use a mobile phone.

examples.ja: この国では、未だに女性の政治家が少ない。
examples.en: In this country, there are still few female politicians.

meaning: how (very) ~; to what extent ~; how to ~
formation: いかに + A / Na / V + か + (が分かる / を知る / を示す)
いかに + V + か (how to do)
いかに + 〜ても (no matter how)
explanation: The written-style counterpart of どんなに, どれほど and どのように. In an embedded question it stresses degree: いかに大切かが分かる "you see just how important it is". It can also ask about manner (いかに生きるか "how to live"). The related forms いかにも ("truly, very much like") and いかが ("how about") are separate words.

examples.ja: 選挙に行って、一票がいかに大切かが分かった。
examples.en: Going to vote made me realize just how important a single vote is.

examples.ja: この数字は、国民が政治にいかに不満を持っているかを示している。
examples.en: These figures show how dissatisfied the public is with politics.

examples.ja: 問題は、限られたお金をいかに使うかである。
examples.en: The question is how to use the limited funds.

meaning: however; nevertheless (formal)
formation: S1。しかしながら、S2。
explanation: A stiff, formal version of しかし used at the start of a sentence in essays, speeches, academic writing and business correspondence. It concedes the previous statement and then presents a contrasting point. In conversation use でも or けれども. ところが introduces an unexpected development rather than a counterargument.

examples.ja: 政府は新しい計画を発表した。しかしながら、国民の理解は得られていない。
examples.en: The government announced a new plan. However, it has not won the public's understanding.

examples.ja: この方法には多くの長所がある。しかしながら、問題がないわけではない。
examples.en: This method has many advantages. Nevertheless, it is not without problems.

meaning: considerably; quite; fairly; a good deal
formation: かなり + A / Na / adverb / V
かなりの + N
explanation: Indicates a degree well above average, though short of the extreme. It sounds objective and works in both speech and writing. ずいぶん adds the speaker's surprise, けっこう is casual and means "more than expected", and なかなか is mostly used for positive evaluations (or with a negative, "not easily"). とても and 非常に are simply "very".

examples.ja: 今回の選挙は、前回よりかなり投票率が高かった。
examples.en: In this election, voter turnout was considerably higher than last time.

examples.ja: この問題を解決するには、かなりの時間がかかるだろう。
examples.en: Solving this problem will probably take a considerable amount of time.

examples.ja: 首相の説明に、かなり多くの人が疑問を持っている。
examples.en: Quite a large number of people have doubts about the prime minister's explanation.

meaning: (someone respected) does ~; honorific use of the passive form
formation: u-verb: V(ない-stem) + れる (話す → 話される, 行く → 行かれる)
ru-verb: stem + られる (出る → 出られる)
する → される; 来る → 来られる
explanation: The passive form doubles as a mild honorific for the actions of someone you respect. It is lighter than お〜になる or special verbs like いらっしゃる, and is common in news, public speaking and workplaces. Because it looks the same as the passive (and the potential of ru-verbs), read the particles: the respected person is the subject and the object keeps を. Never use it for your own actions.

examples.ja: 首相は来週、アメリカを訪問されます。
examples.en: The prime minister will visit the United States next week.

examples.ja: 先生は、この問題についてどう思われますか。
examples.en: Professor, what do you think about this issue?

examples.ja: 社長は毎朝六時に起きられるそうです。
examples.en: I hear the company president gets up at six every morning.

pattern: N 次第だ / N 次第で
meaning: depends on N; depending on N; it is up to N
formation: N + 次第だ (it all depends on N)
N + 次第で(は) (depending on N)
cf. V(ます-stem) + 次第 (as soon as)
explanation: Attached directly to a noun (no の), 次第 says that N is the deciding factor: 努力次第だ "it depends on your effort". N 次第で heads a clause ("depending on N"), and 次第では picks out one possible case. によって is more neutral ("varies according to"). Separate uses to know: V-ます stem + 次第 "as soon as", and 〜次第です, a formal way to explain circumstances.

examples.ja: 合格できるかどうかは、あなたの努力次第だ。
examples.en: Whether you can pass or not depends on your effort.

examples.ja: 選挙の結果次第では、首相が代わるかもしれない。
examples.en: Depending on the election results, the prime minister may be replaced.

examples.ja: 明日の天気次第で、出発の時間を決めましょう。
examples.en: Let us decide the departure time depending on tomorrow's weather.

meaning: not necessarily; it is not always true that
formation: S(plain) + とは限らない
N / Na + (だ)とは限らない
必ずしも / いつも / だれでも / 全部 + … + とは限らない
explanation: Denies that a generalization holds in every case: there are exceptions. It very often appears with 必ずしも, いつも or 全部. 〜わけではない corrects a specific inference the listener might draw, while 〜とは限らない points to exceptions to a general rule. 〜とも限らない with a negative clause ("it may well be that") is a related variant.

examples.ja: お金持ちが必ずしも幸せだとは限らない。
examples.en: Rich people are not necessarily happy.

examples.ja: 新聞に書いてあることが、いつも正しいとは限りません。
examples.en: What is written in the newspaper is not always correct.

examples.ja: 有名な政治家がいい政治家だとは限らない。
examples.en: A famous politician is not necessarily a good politician.

match: とは(限|かぎ)(らない|りません|らず|らなかった)

pattern: ちゃんと / きちんと
meaning: properly; as one should; neatly; without fail
formation: ちゃんと + V
きちんと + V
ちゃんとした / きちんとした + N
explanation: Both adverbs mean doing something the way it ought to be done. ちゃんと is conversational and broad: properly, reliably, really (ちゃんと聞いている). きちんと emphasizes order, accuracy and neatness and is also acceptable in formal contexts. しっかり focuses on firmness and reliability. 〜とした modifies nouns: ちゃんとした仕事 "a proper job".

examples.ja: 約束の時間はちゃんと守ってください。
examples.en: Please make sure to keep to the agreed time.

examples.ja: 彼の部屋は、いつもきちんと片付いている。
examples.en: His room is always neatly tidied up.

examples.ja: 政治家は、国民にきちんと説明する必要がある。
examples.en: Politicians need to explain things properly to the public.

meaning: at least
formation: 少なくとも + quantity + は
少なくとも + N + (だけ)は
少なくとも + S
explanation: Sets a minimum: the real amount may be more, but not less. は after the quantity reinforces the lower limit (三日は "three days at the least"). It can also limit a claim: 少なくとも私は "I, at least". せめて is similar but expresses the speaker's wish for a bare minimum, and 最低(でも) is a blunter "at the very minimum".

examples.ja: この仕事を終えるには、少なくとも三日はかかる。
examples.en: It will take at least three days to finish this job.

examples.ja: 毎日、少なくとも一時間は日本語を勉強している。
examples.en: I study Japanese for at least one hour every day.

examples.ja: 少なくとも私は、その意見に反対です。
examples.en: I, at least, am opposed to that opinion.

meaning: both ~ and ~; there are ~ and also ~
formation: N1 + も + V(ば-form)、N2 + も + V
N1 + も + A-ければ、N2 + も + A
N1 + も + Na / N + なら、N2 + も + Na / N + だ
explanation: Lists two parallel facts to show variety or to pile up points of the same kind, good with good or bad with bad. The ば here is not a condition; it just joins the two halves, much like 〜も〜し、〜も〜. A favorite frame is 〜もあれば〜もある / 〜もいれば〜もいる, "there are some who ... and others who ...".

examples.ja: 人生には、いい時もあれば悪い時もある。
examples.en: In life there are good times and there are bad times.

examples.ja: この店は、値段も安ければ味もいい。
examples.en: At this restaurant the prices are low and the food tastes good too.

examples.ja: 賛成する人もいれば、反対する人もいる。
examples.en: There are people who agree and also people who disagree.

meaning: among; of; out of (a group)
formation: N + のうち(で / の / から)
Number + counter + のうち + Number + counter
N1 と N2 (と N3) + のうち(で)
explanation: Names the whole group from which a part is picked out, either for counting a subset (十人のうち三人 "three out of ten") or for choosing the top item with 一番 or どれ. の中で means the same and is more common in conversation. Do not confuse it with 〜うちに "while" or そのうち "before long".

examples.ja: 十人のうち三人が、その計画に反対した。
examples.en: Three out of the ten people opposed the plan.

examples.ja: この三つの案のうちで、どれが一番いいと思いますか。
examples.en: Of these three proposals, which do you think is best?

examples.ja: クラスの学生のうち、半分以上が留学生です。
examples.en: Of the students in the class, more than half are international students.

match: [^そこあ]のうち(で|の|から|、|[一二三四五六七八九十百千何半0-9０-９])

pattern: 後(の) N / あと + number
meaning: the remaining; the rest of; ~ more (to go)
formation: 後(の) + N (the remaining N)
あと + Number + counter (~ more)
後は + S (as for the rest)
explanation: あと here means what is left over. 後の N is "the rest of the N", and あと三日 means "three more days (to go)"; あと少し is "just a little more". It is usually written in kana in this sense. Keep it apart from 後で "later" and N の後(で) "after N", which refer to order in time.

examples.ja: 十人のうち三人は賛成で、後の七人は反対だった。
examples.en: Of the ten, three were in favor and the remaining seven were against.

examples.ja: 卒業まで、あと三か月しかない。
examples.en: There are only three more months until graduation.

examples.ja: これだけ決めておけば、後のことは心配しなくてもいい。
examples.en: If we decide this much in advance, we need not worry about the rest.

match: あと(の)?[一二三四五六七八九十百千数何0-9０-９]
(あと|[、。はがでて]後)の(こと|人|物|もの|分|時間|仕事|問題|半分|部分|メンバー|学生|[一二三四五六七八九十])

meaning: more than anything; above all
formation: 何より(も) + A / Na / V
N + が / は + 何より(も) + 大切だ / うれしい
何よりの + N
〜て何よりだ (I am so glad that ~)
explanation: A superlative built from 何 + より: "compared with anything else". Use it to single out the most important or most welcome thing. 何よりの N means "the best possible N" (何よりのプレゼント), and 〜て何よりです is a set way to say you are glad about good news. 一番 is the neutral "most"; 何より is more emphatic and emotional.

examples.ja: 健康が何よりも大切だ。
examples.en: Health is more important than anything else.

examples.ja: 平和な世界を作るためには、何より教育が必要だと思う。
examples.en: To build a peaceful world, I think education is needed above all.

examples.ja: 皆さんが無事で、何よりです。
examples.en: I am so glad that everyone is safe.

meaning: as ~ (changes); in accordance with; following
formation: V(dictionary; change) + に従って / に従い
N(change) + に従って
N(rule / instruction / person) + に従って (in accordance with)
explanation: Two uses: (1) proportional change, "as X progresses, Y changes", like につれて; (2) acting in obedience to instructions, rules or a person. につれて has only the first meaning, and unlike につれて, に従って can be followed by an intentional action. に従い is the more formal written form. Sentence-initial したがって means "therefore".

examples.ja: 科学が進歩するに従って、人々の生活は便利になった。
examples.en: As science has advanced, people's lives have become more convenient.

examples.ja: 係の人の指示に従って、行動してください。
examples.en: Please act in accordance with the instructions of the staff.

examples.ja: 人口が増えるに従い、食料の問題が深刻になるだろう。
examples.en: As the population grows, the food problem will likely become serious.

meaning: only; just; a mere ~
formation: たった(の) + Number + counter
たった + Number + counter + で / しか〜ない / だけ
たった今 (just now)
explanation: Placed before a number, たった stresses that the amount is small: たった五人 "a mere five people". だけ comes after the quantity and the two can be combined (たった一人だけ). It needs a quantity or 今, so it cannot be put before an ordinary noun (×たった水). Do not confuse it with the past forms 立った or 経った.

examples.ja: たった一週間で、町の様子がすっかり変わってしまった。
examples.en: In just one week, the look of the town changed completely.

examples.ja: 参加者はたったの五人だった。
examples.en: There were a mere five participants.

examples.ja: たった一度の人生だから、好きなことをしたい。
examples.en: You only live once, so I want to do what I love.

match: たった(の)?[一二三四五六七八九十百千数0-9０-９今ひふ]

pattern: 〜てしかたがない / 〜てしょうがない
romaji: te shikata ga nai / te shou ga nai
meaning: cannot help feeling ~; unbearably ~; so ~ I cannot stand it
formation: A-くて + しかたがない
Na-で + しかたがない
V(て; feeling / desire: 〜たくて, 気になって) + しかたがない
〜て + しようがない / しょうがない (colloquial)
explanation: Expresses a feeling, desire or bodily sensation so strong that the speaker cannot control it. It describes the speaker; for a third person add ようだ or らしい. 〜てたまらない is very close, and 〜てならない is a more written variant. On its own, しかたがない / しょうがない means "it cannot be helped", which is a different use.

examples.ja: 国の家族に会いたくてしかたがない。
examples.en: I am dying to see my family back home.

examples.ja: 昨日あまり寝ていないので、眠くてしょうがない。
examples.en: I did not sleep much last night, so I am unbearably sleepy.

examples.ja: 試験の結果が気になってしようがない。
examples.en: I cannot stop worrying about the exam results.

keywords: so much i cannot stand it
match: (て|で)(しかた|仕方)(が)?(ない|ありません|なかった)
(て|で)(しょう|しよう)が(ない|ありません|なかった)

meaning: since ~ (continuously up to now)
formation: V(て) + 以来
N + 以来
explanation: Marks a past point from which a state or repeated situation has continued right up to the present. The main clause describes something ongoing, not a single later event, and it is not used for the very recent past or for the future. 〜てから simply orders two events; 〜て以来 insists on "ever since then".

examples.ja: 日本に来て以来、一度も国に帰っていない。
examples.en: I have not been back to my country even once since coming to Japan.

examples.ja: 卒業以来、彼とは会っていません。
examples.en: I have not seen him since graduation.

examples.ja: インターネットが広まって以来、世界の情報がすぐに手に入るようになった。
examples.en: Ever since the internet spread, information from around the world has become instantly available.

meaning: everything; from A to Z; in every respect
formation: 何から何まで + V / A
何から何まで + N + だ
explanation: Literally "from what to what": absolutely everything, without exception. It works as an adverb and is more emphatic and colloquial than 全部 or すべて. It is often used to thank someone for doing everything, or to stress that two things differ or match in every respect.

examples.ja: 引っ越しの時は、友達に何から何まで手伝ってもらった。
examples.en: When I moved, my friend helped me with absolutely everything.

examples.ja: あの二人は、考え方が何から何まで違う。
examples.en: Those two differ in their way of thinking in every respect.

examples.ja: この国では、何から何まで機械がやってくれる。
examples.en: In this country, machines do everything for you, from A to Z.

meaning: on the contrary; instead; (ended up) all the more
formation: (S1 て / と / たら / が、) かえって + S2
explanation: Shows that the result is the reverse of what was intended or expected: you did something to improve matters and things got worse (or the other way round). むしろ expresses a preference between two options ("rather"), and 逆に is a broader "conversely". Written 却って; do not confuse it with 帰って, the て-form of 帰る.

examples.ja: 薬を飲んだら、かえって具合が悪くなった。
examples.en: I took the medicine, and it actually made me feel worse.

examples.ja: 急いでタクシーに乗ったが、道が込んでいて、かえって遅くなってしまった。
examples.en: I took a taxi because I was in a hurry, but the roads were crowded and I ended up even later.

examples.ja: 便利な物が増えて、かえって忙しくなった気がする。
examples.en: With more convenient things around, I feel we have become busier instead.

meaning: at the same time as; the moment ~; as well as (being)
formation: V(dictionary / た) + と同時に
N + と同時に
A-い / Na・N + である + と同時に
explanation: Two uses: (1) two events take place at the same moment, or one immediately on the other ("the moment the bell rang"); (2) two qualities or roles coexist ("convenient and at the same time dangerous"). と共に overlaps but is also used for gradual change. 〜たとたん(に) stresses a sudden, unexpected follow-up.

examples.ja: ベルが鳴ると同時に、学生たちは教室を出ていった。
examples.en: The moment the bell rang, the students left the classroom.

examples.ja: 卒業と同時に、東京の会社に就職した。
examples.en: Upon graduating, I took a job at a company in Tokyo.

examples.ja: 科学の進歩は生活を便利にすると同時に、新しい問題も生んでいる。
examples.en: Scientific progress makes life convenient and at the same time creates new problems.

meaning: ... was it?; what was ~ again? (trying to recall)
formation: V / A (た-form) + っけ
N / Na + だ(った) + っけ
〜でしたっけ / 〜ましたっけ (polite)
〜んだっけ
explanation: A casual sentence-ending used when you are trying to remember something you once knew, or checking a half-remembered fact with the listener. It can also be said to oneself when reminiscing (よく遊んだっけ). It is not for asking about something entirely new to you. With friends use だっけ / たっけ; でしたっけ makes it polite enough for acquaintances.

examples.ja: 明日の会議は何時からだっけ。
examples.en: What time does tomorrow's meeting start again?

examples.ja: この映画、前に一緒に見たっけ。
examples.en: Did we watch this movie together before?

examples.ja: すみません、お名前は何でしたっけ。
examples.en: Sorry, what was your name again?

meaning: leave ~ (on, open, undone); keep ~ing nonstop
formation: V(ます-stem) + っぱなし + だ / で
V(ます-stem) + っぱなし + に + する
V(ます-stem) + っぱなし + の + N
explanation: Two uses: (1) something is left in a state without the follow-up it should get, with a critical tone (電気をつけっぱなし "leaving the light on"); (2) the same action or state goes on without a break (立ちっぱなし "standing the whole time"). 〜たまま is neutral about an unchanged state, while 〜っぱなし is colloquial and usually negative.

examples.ja: 電気をつけっぱなしで寝てしまった。
examples.en: I fell asleep with the lights left on.

examples.ja: 電車が込んでいて、東京までずっと立ちっぱなしだった。
examples.en: The train was crowded, and I was on my feet the whole way to Tokyo.

examples.ja: 水を出しっぱなしにしないでください。
examples.en: Please do not leave the water running.
